en: Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa. One should worship that elephant-faced one, who has a slightly reddish luster, three eyes, and a broad belly; who holds the Vedas in his hands and bears a crescent moon upon the region of his head; who carries a jar from which flows a stream of nectar; who is served by all the exalted immortals beginning with Brahmā and Indra; who possesses white teeth; who is surrounded by the lords of serpents and other auspicious beings; and who brings about every kind of welfare. (1) I bow to the Daughter of the Mountain, whose body is like the rising sun, who has made her home in the left side of the Destroyer of Cities (Śiva), who fulfills the desires of her devotees, and who is praised by the gods. (2) [She] whose beautiful crown is adorned with a digit of the moon and who is entwined by the Śaivala creeper...

I bow to the daughter of the Lord of Mountains, whose face surpasses the beauty of the moon on the eighth day, who has eyes like blue lotuses, and who holds a rosary, arrows, a bowstring, and a goad in her exceedingly tender arms; she who is beautiful in every limb and possesses a soft, radiant luster. I bow to Mukunda, the repository of all virtues, who is constantly surrounded by groups of young sages delighted by the play upon the charming banks of the Yamunā; he who is the abode of all scriptures that destroy the fear of the entire universe through his divine sports, and the beautiful root of the great tree of worldly existence.

May the son of Mukuṇda, whose majesty delights the hearts of all people, who subdues the pride of the lordly elephant [of the senses], and who is surrounded by a multitude of restless glances, grant me peace. (4) I worship that Sun whom I have quickly taken as my refuge—he at whose rising the multitudes of lotuses bloom, the ruddy geese sport, birds wander at will in all directions, students recite their lessons, and auspiciousness prevails in the world. (6) He who, being the lame charioteer, mounted his single-wheeled chariot and yoked there the seven horses... (5)

I bow with devotion to that Śiva, the destroyer of Māra, who—though his deeds throughout the three worlds were exceedingly wondrous and he possessed seven bodies through his powers of illusion—nevertheless, by means of the flower-arrows that agitate even the minds of yogis, quickly quelled with the fire of his eye that Māra who was tormenting even those of great strength. (7–8) [I bow] to the body of Dhūrjaṭi, which strikes the surface of the earth with its moving feet, which is adorned with the excellent water of the flowing Gaṅgā, whose three terrifying eyes are rolling, and whose mass of matted hair pierces the clouds moving above. (9)

May this ever-new auspiciousness of mine, a *tupatutaṇḍava*, flourish! (9) There was the illustrious Śrīnivāsakṛti, the best of the wise, who was a cage for the parrots of the scriptures and traditional teachings; who brought joy to the assembly of the virtuous; who was a servant to the Goddess of Fortune, the beloved of the moon (the repository of arts); who was praised by the entire multitude of the learned, being an expert in the various branches of learning, in poetic composition, and in the collection of diverse sciences; and whose charming offspring were wiped upon the expansive foreheads of all kings. He was the Mount Mandara for churning the ocean of all the Agamas. (10) The illustrious... [text ends]... whose power was pleasing as it was rubbed against the network of the broad foreheads of all monarchs.

The son of Śrīnivāsa is Jagannivāsa; his virtuous sons, whose hearts are moist with compassion, are bees at the lotus-feet of the Daughter of the Mountain King (Pārvatī). The eldest is renowned as Śiromaṇi, and the youngest after him is indeed Cakrapāṇi, known by the name Janārdana. Among them, Janārdana, out of curiosity according to his own intellect and for the sake of enlightening the son of Tāntrika, composes this *Mantracandrikā*. Whatever mantras were revealed here in the *Śivārcanacandrikā* by the work of the illustrious Śrīnivāsa—

All these have been composed through the contemplation of the Sage and endowed with the six ancillaries (*ṣaḍaṅga*); I shall now properly declare them without prolixity. (14) First are the mantras of Gaṇapati, then those of Śivā, thereafter those of Kṛṣṇa, Sūrya, and Śambhu, as they are traditionally taught in due order. (15) Now, having recollected Gaṇeśa and the others in sequence, their mantras and the divisions of those mantras are being written down. Herein are the mantras of Gaṇeśa; first among them is the single-syllable mantra of Gaṇeśa: *git*. Having performed three breath-restraints (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *git* Gaṇeśa mantra, [one should place] *oṃ ga* on the head...

Salutation to the *Ṛṣi* Nakāya at the face; salutation to the *Chandas* Nivṛt at the mouth; salutation to the *Devatā* Vighneśvara at the heart; salutation to the *Bīja* Brahma at the secret place; salutation to the *Śakti* Māyā at the two feet. Again, salutation to the *Bīja* Paramātman at the secret place; salutation to the *Śakti* Buddhi at the two feet. Again, salutation to the *Bīja* Udāna at the secret place; salutation to the *Śakti* Kuṇḍalinī at the two feet. Again, salutation to the *Bīja* Ga at the secret place; salutation to the *Śakti* Bindu at that very spot. Salutation to the *Kīlaka* Nāda at the navel. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), the application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of attaining all my desired goals. (Thus, with palms joined...)

Having performed the purification of the hands with the root mantra *liruk*, one should assign the mantras to the fingers from the thumbs to the little fingers as follows: *Oṃ gaṇaṃjayāya svāhā*—to the heart, *namaḥ*, on the two thumbs; *Ekadaṃṣṭrāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—to the head, *vaṣaṭ*, on the two index fingers; *Acalakarṇine namaḥ*—to the tuft (*śikhā*), *huṃ*, on the two middle fingers; *Gajavaktrāya namo namaḥ*—to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*, on the two ring fingers;

*Mahodarāya caṇḍāya huṃ phaṭ*—to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*, on the two little fingers. Having thus assigned these mantras to both hands from the thumbs to the little fingers, one should perform the assignment to the five parts of the body, starting from the heart, excluding the eyes.

One should also perform the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) upon the limbs using the seed-syllable *gaṃ gīṃ gūṃ*, which possesses the six long vowels. Now, for the meditation (*dhyāna*): May that Lord Vighnarāja, the King of Obstacles, become present for the welfare of all beings—he who has red limbs, garments, and flowers; who is adorned with rice-grains; who bears the moon upon his crest; who is endowed with three eyes; whose hands and feet are short; whose nose is shaped like a citron (*vījapūra*); who holds a noose and a goad at the tips of his hands, while granting boons and protection; who has the face of a serpent; who is adorned with snakes; and who sits in the lotus posture. [The seed-syllables are assigned] to the left and right upper [arms], and then to those below them, starting from the first.

Having performed the meditation on the weapons with "Oṃ raṇye," and having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having again performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should offer the water held in the hand while reciting: "O you who are the protector of the most secret of secrets, accept this *japa* performed by us; may there be success for me, O God, through your grace, for you abide within me. Then one should prostrate. This is the procedure for the six-limbed meditation on the single-syllable Gaṇeśa. There are other six variations of this very mantra: *gaṃ*, *gaḥ*, *gauṃ*, *gaḥ*, *glau*, *goḥ*. Among these, for the two seed-syllables *glau* and *gam*, the word *gaṇa* [is applied].

He is known as *Kumārī-rakta*, possesses the *Anuṣṭubh* meter, and has the Sun as his deity. He is praised by the Gaṇas and is saluted by all gods and demons. One should fashion the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with his own mantra joined with the six long vowels.

Here, it should be understood that the placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) consists of *glāṃ glīṃ* and so forth for the first [limb], and *gāṃ gīṃ* and so forth for the second. His meditation, worship, recitation (*japa*), and other rites should be performed just as before.
Thus, this single-syllable mantra, when combined, is of seven types. Now, the mantra of Virigaṇeśa consists of twenty-six syllables: *hrīṃ viri viriga*.

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas* with the mantra: "O best of lords of Gaṇas, granter of boons, bring all the world under my control, svāhā," one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the sage Gaṇaka at the head; salutation to the *gāyatrī* metre at the mouth; salutation to the deity Vighneśvara at the heart. Having stated, "This is the application for the attainment of desired success" with palms joined in reverence, one recites: "Hrīṃ vira vira, salutation to the heart; Hrīṃ Gaṇapati, svāhā to the head; Hrīṃ Varavarada, vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair; Hrīṃ Sarvalokam me, huṃ to the armor; Hrīṃ va..."

Having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) with the mantras: *Śamānayanetrāya vaṣaṭ*, *Hrīṃ svāhā astrāya phaṭ*, one should assign them from the thumb to the palms of the hands, and then likewise assign them to the heart and other centers.

Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*): I worship [the Lord] who has the luster of vermilion, an elephant face, and three eyes; who holds a noose and a goad in his hands, and constantly bears a honey-filled skull-cup; whose head is crowned by the crescent moon; whose body is embraced by Puṣpā; whose hand rests upon the lotus-like organ shining at the tip of his banner; and whose left hand begins from the raised right hand, sprinkling pure water from a vessel filled with excellent lotuses.

The visualization of the weapons is as follows: from the right hand up to the waist, there are three nooses; the left lower hand rests on the shoulder of the Goddess; with his right hand, he embraces the beloved Goddess who is seated upon his left lap; with his left lower hand, he touches the tip of the banner; and in his left and right [upper hands] are lotuses. The trunk is the stalk. Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having again performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should offer the recitation with the previously mentioned mantra beginning "O secret of secrets... and prostrate. Some [recite] this mantra nineteen times...

In their opinion, they say that [the mantra] consists of true syllables; thus, "Varavarade" (O giver of boons) consists of five syllables, and "Lokam" (the world) consists of two syllables, so there are no fewer syllables. For this mantra as well, the visualization of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and so forth is exactly like the previous mantra. Since this is stated as another form of the previously mentioned mantra beginning with *Māyā* (Hrīṃ), there is a specific distinction in its visualization: holding a *bījāpūra* fruit, a goad, a lotus seat, and a garland of enemies with her left hands, and holding a noose, an arrow, a bow, and a jewel-filled jar with her right hands; her body is red as vermilion, and she has three eyes.

The host of Gaṇas, with trunks bent down and raised, holding lotuses in their hands, carry Puṣṭi (Nourishment) from the front; here, the visualization of the weapons begins from the lower left hand and proceeds to the lower right hand, because the pitcher is joined to all the upper hands. This is the visualization. The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and so forth are as in the previous mantra. Thus are the three mantras of Virigaṇapati. Now, Lakṣmīgaṇeśa: *Śrīṃ gaṃ saumyāya mahāgaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā*. This is the twenty-nine-syllable mantra.

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas*, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the Seer Antaryāmin at the head; salutation to the *Nivṛt* Gāyatrī metre at the mouth; salutation to the Deity Śrī Lakṣmī at the heart. Having thus performed the placement, one should perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) on the hands and body with: "Oṃ Śrīṃ Gāṃ, salutation to the Heart; Oṃ Śrīṃ Gīṃ, Svāhā to the Head; Oṃ Śūṃ Gūṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the Tuft of Hair; Oṃ Śraiḥ Gauṃ, Huṃ to the Armor; Oṃ Śrauḥ Gauṃ, Vauṣaṭ to the Eyes; Oṃ Śraḥ Maḥ, Phaṭ to the Weapon. Having thus performed the ritual placement, one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "Golden-hued, wearing yellow garments..."

May He who joins the discus and conch with ruby lotuses, who holds the goad and the gesture of fearlessness, whose nose is adorned with a golden jar, who is seated upon a lotus, who has three eyes, who is embraced by Lakṣmī resting on his left lap while she holds a lotus, and who—embraced by her with her right hand—possesses a golden luster that bestows great prosperity upon the hosts of Gaṇas; may He grant you glory. Having meditated thus, having performed the recitation (*japa*), and having offered the prayer, one should prostrate. Thus ends the section on Lakṣmī-Gaṇeśa. *Note regarding the description of weapons:* Starting from the upper right hand and proceeding down to the lower right hand, the trunk of the elephant's nose serves as the handle for the weapons. Having meditated thus, having performed the recitation, and having offered [the oblation], one should prostrate. Thus ends the section on Lakṣmī-Gaṇeśa.

Now, for the *Śama-mantra*: the Lord of Gaṇas, whose power resides in the syllables, [is worshipped] with the mantra *hrīṃ gnīṃ hrīṃ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Oṃ, salutation to Bhārgava, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; Oṃ, to Virāṭ, the Meter (*chandas*), on the face; Oṃ, salutation to the Deity Śrī-Śakti-Gaṇapati, on the heart. Having thus performed the placement, and having executed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *gāṃ gīṃ* and so forth, one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "The Lord who has the face of the king of elephants, with ears flapping, beautiful cheeks, golden complexion, and four arms; the all-pervading one holding a noose and a goad, [and bestowing] his own..."

One should meditate upon Him holding a *vījapūra* (citron) in His right hand and a sweetmeat (*moḍaka*) in His left hand. This meditation on the weapons begins from the upper left hand and extends down to the lower left hand.
Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*), one should offer it. Now follows the four-syllabled mantra of Śaktigaṇapati: *Oṃ hrīṃ grīṃ hrīṃ*.

Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ śukāya ṛṣaye namaḥ* on the head; *Oṃ gāyatrīchandase namaḥ* on the mouth; *Oṃ* on the heart.

Having performed the placement [of mantras] with "Oṃ śaktigaṇapataye devatāyai namaḥ" and having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) starting with "Gāṃ gīṃ," etc., one should perform the visualization (*dhyāna*) as follows: "One should meditate upon Śrī Gaṇeśa—the Lord of Wisdom, the refuge of the three worlds, and the one worshipped by the universe—who is golden-hued, wears golden garments, has a large belly and slender body, beautiful arms, and three eyes; who holds in his hands a noose, a rosary, his own tusk, a goad, and a sweetmeat (*modaka*) in his trunk; who is adorned with golden ornaments, possesses a beautiful *śakti* (spear) as radiant as the rising sun, and is peerless. [The visualization proceeds] beginning from the upper right hand... to the left.

Having meditated on the visualization of the weapons up to the top of the head (*mūrdhakaraparyantam*), and having performed the recitation (*japa*) and offered that recitation to the Deity, one should prostrate. Thus ends the four-syllabled *Śakti-Gaṇapati*.

Now follows the ten-syllabled mantra for swift propitiation: "Gaṃ kṣipraprasādanāya namaḥ. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Oṃ gaṇakāya ṛṣaye namaḥ" on the head; "Oṃ virāṭ chandase namaḥ" on the mouth; and "Oṃ kṣipraprasādanāya gaṇapataye devatāyai namaḥ" on the heart.

Having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the mantra beginning with *gāṃgīm* and so forth, one should perform meditation as follows: "Holding a noose, a goad, a wish-fulfilling creeper, and a tusk in [his four] trunks, bearing a citron fruit, red in color, three-eyed, with the young moon upon his crest, radiant with necklaces, elephant-faced, and bestowing boons—[thus is he]. The visualization of the weapons begins from the upper left trunk and extends to the lower left hand. Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*), one should offer it. This is the ten-syllable mantra for the swift propitiation of Gaṇeśa. Now, Heraṃba-Gaṇeśa...

Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the mantra *oṃ gūṃ namaḥ*, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: *oṃ gaṇakāya ṛṣaye namaḥ* on the head; *oṃ gāyatrī chandase namaḥ* on the mouth; and *oṃ śrīherambāya devatāyai namaḥ* on the heart. Then, having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) beginning with *gāṃ gīṃ* and so forth, one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows:

"Heramba is to be meditated upon with five serpent-faces resembling pearls, lightning, clouds, nectar, and saffron; he wears the moon upon his crown and is mounted upon a proud lion, [holding] in his hands..."

Having meditated thus: [the deity] holding a trident, goad, lotus, rosary, mace, a human head, and axe; with a sweetmeat (modaka) in the left hand and granting fearlessness in the right; possessing the brilliance of a multitude of suns; with the gestures of boon-granting and fearlessness in the lower left and right hands; above those, hands bestowing sweetmeats; above those, an axe and a skull-cup; above those, a rosary and a mace; and above those, a goad and a trident.

"Having performed the recitation (*japa*), one should offer it. Thus ends the mantra of Heraṃba Gaṇeśa. Now follows the mantra of Subrahmaṇya Gaṇeśa: "Oṃ vacatbhuve namaḥ. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with this seven-syllable mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Oṃ agnaye ṛṣaye namaḥ" on the head; "Gāyatrīchandase" on the mouth; "Subrahmaṇyāya devatāyai namaḥ" on the heart.

Then, having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) starting with "Rāṃ rīṃ," etc., one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "May he whose form is tawny protect [us]... [and so on]. O Moon... [text continues].

Holding a lotus, a fear-dispelling [mace], a spear that destroys enemies, and an auspicious cock with his arms, smeared with red unguents, wearing red garments and garlands, adorned with various ornaments, the Lord of the Gaṇas, Subrahmaṇya, the bringer of welfare and destroyer of obstacles at the outset—[he is meditated upon] with the first two hands below and the other two above. This is the visualization of the weapons.

Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should offer it. If this mantra ends with the *praṇava* (Oṃ), it consists of eight syllables; if the *praṇava* is at the beginning, [it consists of nine].

If the seed-syllable of Śakti (*śrīṃ*) is added, then there is another eight-syllabled mantra; thus, this mantra is threefold. This concludes the mantra of Subrahmaṇya Gaṇeśa. Now follows the mantra of Śrī Mahāgaṇapati:

*Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye vara-varada sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this twenty-eight-syllabled mantra, one should perform the placement of mantras (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ gaṇakāya ṛṣaye namaḥ* on the head; *Oṃ nivṛt gāyatrī chandase namaḥ* on the mouth; *Oṃ* on the heart... [and so forth].

Salutation to the deity Śrī Mahāgaṇapati. Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Oṃ Gaṃ, salutation to the seed-syllable (*bīja*) on the private parts; Hrīṃ, salutation to the power (*śakti*) on the feet," and having declared with palms joined, "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of all my desired goals," [one should proceed]: "Oṃ Gāṃ, salutation to the heart; Oṃ Śrīṃ Gīṃ, Svāhā to the head; Oṃ Hrīṃ Guṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (*śikhā*); Oṃ Klīṃ Gaiṃ, Huṃ to the armor (*kavaca*); Oṃ Glauṃ Gauṃ, Vauṣaṭ to the eyes; Oṃ Gaṃ Gaḥ, Phaṭ to the weapon (*astra*). Having thus placed these six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) on the two hands from the thumbs to the little fingers, [one should place them] at the heart.

One should also perform the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the six limbs beginning with compassion (*dayā*). Then: *oṃ namaḥ* in the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*); *śrīṃ namaḥ* in the right ear; *hrīṃ* in the left [ear]; *klīṃ* in the right eye; *glauḥ* in the left [eye]; *gaṃ* in the right nostril; *gaṃ* in the left nostril; *ṇaṃ* in the mouth; *yaḥ* at the base of the right arm; *taṃ* in the middle [of the forearm]; *yaṃ* at the wrist (*maṇibandha*); *vaṃ* at the base of the fingers; *raṃ* at the base of the left arm; *vaṃ* in the middle [of the forearm];

*raṃ* at the wrist; *daṃ* at the base of the fingers; *saṃ* on the right thigh; *vaṃ* on the right knee; *jaṃ* on the right ankle; *naṃ* at the base of the toes of the right foot; *meṃ* on the left thigh; *vaṃ* on the left knee; [the rest] on the left...

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: *māṃ* at the root of the toes of the left foot; *naṃ* at the *anāhata*; *yaṃ* at the *maṇipūra*; *svāṃ* at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*; *hāṃ* at the *mūlādhāra*; *oṃ* on the head; *śrīṃ* on the face; *hrīṃ* in the heart; *klīṃ* in the anus; *glauṃ* on the feet; and *gaṃ namaḥ* in the heart—then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with the twenty-two syllables beginning with *gaṇapataye* from the head down to the feet, [one should place]: *śrīṃ* on the face, saying "Salutation to Śrī and Śrīpati"; *hrīṃ* in the heart, saying "To Gaurī and Gaurīpati"; and *oṃ klīṃ* in the secret place, saying "To Rati and Kāma"; [and] on the feet.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: *Līṃ Lauṃ* to the face for Mahī and Varāha; *Oṃ Gaṃ* to the heart for Āmoda and Siddhi; *Oṃ Gaṃ* to the private parts for Pramoda and Samṛddhi; *Oṃ Gaṃ* to the two feet for Sumukha and Kānti; *Oṃ Gaṃ* to the heart for Durmukha and Madanāvanī; *Ne Gaṃ* to the knees for Vighnakartṛ and Ḍāviṇī, followed by *Namaḥ*—one should then perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows:
"On an auspicious island made of nine jewels in the ocean of blood, its pure bottom washed by the water shimmering with waves, [there stands] a mass of spray..."

One should meditate upon that Pārijāta, the wish-fulfilling tree, in its center—a place frequented by pleasant fragrant breezes, adorned with regions beautified by wish-fulfilling trees (kalpavṛkṣas), crowded with various flowers, resplendent with diverse birds, filled with many fruits, and surrounded by throngs of Apsaras; a place filled with the light of rising morning sunshine and the moonlight of the moon, its ground made crimson by the floor of shimmering rubies, and made sweet by the humming of bees resting on the blossoms of the wish-fulfilling trees. One should contemplate it all at once.

One should meditate upon a lion-throne made of the nine gems, adorned with flowers and covered with a silken cloth, beneath which is a lotus of letters with six petals; in its center, within the pericarp, is a triangle where resides the Great Gaṇa. He has the face of an elephant with a single tusk, enriched with various jewel ornaments. With his hands, he holds a discus, a trident, a bow of sugarcane, a red lotus, a mace, a vessel filled with the tips of rice grains, and a citron. He is embraced by his own consort, who raises a lotus in her hand, and he is as radiant as the *japā* flower.

One should worship Gaṇapati with all ritual offerings after meditating upon him as follows: he who is half the size of the moon, resplendent with three eyes, holding at his mouth a jar from which flows a mass of jewels gathered from the ocean; he who constantly showers gems, pearls, coral, and other treasures in every direction; before whom the practitioner stands, while swarms of bees greedy for the water of his own gift repeatedly ward him off with the flapping of his ears; he who is served by gods and demons, whose crown is radiant, whose belly is large, who has the face of an elephant, and is adorned with various ornaments. Having thus meditated, one should worship Gaṇapati with all ritual services.

The visualization of the weapons is as follows: in the upper two lotuses are discs; below those, a trident and a noose; below that, a bow and a blue lotus; below that, a mace and a grain of rice; below that, a citron and two teeth; and at the tip of the trunk, a food-pot. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having performed the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), one should offer the recitation to the Deity and prostrate.
Some, however, omit the dative case of the word "Gaṇapataye" and say "Gaṇapate" in the vocative case; in that case, this [mantra] consists of twenty-six syllables.

The mantra is as follows: "In this regard, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) and other rites according to the instruction. This is the Mahāgaṇapati mantra. Now, the Trailokyamohana mantra: *vakratuṇḍaikadaṃṣṭrāya klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṃ gaṇapati varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā*. Having performed three breath-retentions (*prāṇāyāma*) with this thirty-three-syllable mantra, one should place [the mantras] on the head: *oṃ gaṃ gaṇakāya ṛṣaye namaḥ*; on the mouth: *gāyatrāya chandase*; and on the heart: *oṃ trailokyamohanāya gaṇapate*.

Having assigned the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other components with "teyedevatāyai," one should say with palms joined in reverence, "viniyogaḥ" for the attainment of my desired goal. Then: *vakratuṇḍaikadaṃṣṭrāya klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *gaṃ gaṇapataye śirase svāhā*; *varavarada śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*; *sarvajanaṃ kavacāya huṃ*; *me vaśamānaya netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*; *svāhā astrāya phaṭ*. Having thus assigned these six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) from the thumbs to the palms of both hands, [one assigns them] to the six limbs beginning with the heart.

Even while sleeping, one should perform meditation as follows: "In the ocean of milk... and so forth, meditating upon [the deity] like Āditya Mahāgaṇeśa. Having performed the recitation (*japa*) and offered it, one should prostrate to the venerable Guru and the Deity. Thus ends Trailokyamohana Gaṇeśa. Now, for the twelve-syllabled Śakti-Gaṇeśa: *Hrīṃ Gaṃ Hrīṃ Mahāgaṇapataye Svāhā*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should offer salutations: to the sage Gaṇaka at the head; to the Nivṛt-Gāyatrī meter at the mouth; and to the heart at the chest.

"Obeisance to the deity Śrī Śaktigaṇeśa"—having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*), [one says] "this is the application for the attainment of all my desired goals. With palms joined in reverence, one recites: *Hrīṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *Gaṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *Hrīṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*; to Mahāgaṇapati, the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ svāhā*; to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; and with the *Sama-sūma* mantra, to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. Having thus performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*), one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: [He who possesses] the luster of pearls and the moon, who bears the crescent of the moon, whose eye is on his forehead, and who is beautiful.

One should take refuge in the one who wears a crown of clusters of jewels; who holds in his lotus-hands a lotus, a goad, and a large vessel of nectar; whose beloved stands upon his own playful lap with her beautiful feet placed upon his banner;
and whose hand is placed within the womb of that beloved. (This is the meditation on the lotus and other attributes, starting from the lower right hand up to the lower left hand.

Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's ability, one should offer worship to the God. This is the twelve-syllable Śakti-Gaṇeśa. Now follows the eleven-syllable [mantra].

For Śaktigaṇeśa, having performed three rounds of *prāṇāyāma* with the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ gaṃ hrīṃ vaśamānaya svāhā," and having assigned the sage (*muni*) and other elements as prescribed for the twelve-syllable mantra, one should assign the six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) as follows: "Oṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ" (to the heart), "hrīṃ gaṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā" (to the head), "vaśaṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ" (to the tuft of hair), "ānaya kavacāya huṃ" (to the armor), "svāhā netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ" (to the eyes), and "samastamantraṇāstrāya phaṭ" (to the weapon). Having thus assigned these to the hands from the thumb to the little finger, one should likewise assign them to the six limbs beginning with the heart.

One should meditate upon the Lord who is worthy of worship: whose complexion is like that of the *bandhūka* flower; who has three eyes and a moon upon his crest; who is Gaṇeśa, fond of enjoyments; who holds in his trunk-tips a serpent-mouthed goad, a boon-granting gesture, and a sugarcane staff; who is embraced by that dark-limbed woman who touches his linga—she who is the abode of passion (*madana*)—while he himself holds a lotus;

and [one should meditate on] the visualization of the weapons starting from the upper left hand down to the lower right hand. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*), one should offer it. This is the [meditation on] the eleven-syllable Śakti-mantra.

The mantra of Gaṇeśa: Now, for Haridrā-Gaṇeśa: *Oṃ huṃ gaṃ glauṃ, O Haridrā-Gaṇapati, bestower of boons, paralyze, paralyze the hearts of all people, svāhā!* Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this thirty-two-syllable mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), saying: "Salutation to Madana, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Anuṣṭubh, the meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to the deity Haridrā-Gaṇapati, on the heart. Then, with palms joined in reverence, one should state the application: "For the attainment of all my desired goals, this is the application (*viniyoga*)," and recite *gāṃ gīm*, etc., and *glāṃ glīm*, etc.

Having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) from the feet upwards, one should meditate as follows: "I worship Him who is seated upon a jewel-encrusted lion-throne in the previously described place; who is yellow in complexion, adorned with yellow ornaments, and beautified by excellent, shimmering garlands and other finery; whose face is gentle and smiling, who is radiant with three eyes, and who holds in His hands the noose (*pāśa*), the excellent axe (*paraśu*), the boon-granting gesture (*vara*), and the goad (*aṅkuśa*), along with the *krodha-mudrā* and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*). In the three left hands, starting from the uppermost, are the first three [implements], and in the three right hands, starting from the uppermost, are the other three. Thus, having contemplated Him in this manner, one should perform the recitation (*japa*). (Note on the implements: The *krodha-mudrā* is formed by the fist; thus, the sequence of weapons is: noose, axe, boon-gesture, goad, *krodha-mudrā*, and fearlessness.)

"May [the deity] bestow [blessings] upon you"—thus ends the *Haridrā-Gaṇapati-mantra*. Now, for the *Vakratuṇḍa-Gaṇeśa-mantra*: having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the six-syllable mantra "Vakratuṇḍāya Huṃ," one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Bhārgava, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Anuṣṭubh, the Meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to Vakratuṇḍa, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart.

Then: "Salutation to the Heart (*hṛdaya*); Svāhā to the Head (*śiras*); Vaṣaṭ to the Crest (*śikhā*); Huṃ to the Armor (*kavaca*); Vauṣaṭ to the Eye (*netra*); and with the entire mantra, Phaṭ to the Weapon (*astra*)."

Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the six-limbed mantras from the thumbs to the palms of both hands, and having also performed the placement upon the six limbs beginning with the heart, one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "One should meditate upon this Vakratuṇḍa, who possesses three eyes, is endowed with a red garland, garments, and ornaments, and holds in his sprout-like hands the noose, the goad, the boon-granting gesture (*abhaya*), and the wish-granting gesture (*iṣṭa*). He shines with a luster emerging from a beautiful, reddish-red jewel-mine, and stands within the opening of a blooming lotus. The visualization of the weapons is as follows: the first two [weapons] are in the left and right upper hands; the other two are in those situated below the first two, respectively. Thus ends the meditation.

Having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity and offered it, one should prostrate. In this regard, some say that the syllable *hūm* should be pronounced long; here, the recitation and other rites should be performed according to the instruction of one’s guru. This concludes the six-syllabled *Vakratuṇḍa-Gaṇeśa* mantra: *meghāṃlkāya svāhā*. Having performed the breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) three times with the root mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Bhārgava-ṛṣi" on the head; "Salutation to Anuṣṭubh-chandas" on the mouth; and "Salutation to Vakratuṇḍa-devatā" on the heart.

One should perform the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the six mantra-syllables; however, the meditation (*dhyāna*) and other rites are exactly as previously stated for the mantra. This is the second Vakratuṇḍa mantra. Now follows the thirty-two syllable Atharvaṇika mantra: *rāyasyoṣasya dayitā nidhi do ratnado mataḥ rakṣohaṇo vovalagahano vakratuṇḍāya huṃ*. The seer (*ṛṣi*), meditation, and other details are like those of the previously mentioned six-syllable mantra. This is the Atharvaṇika mantra. Now follows the Ucchiṣṭagaṇeśa mantra: *hastipiśācilikhesvāhā*. Thus [ends the section].

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas* with the mantra consisting of the syllables [of the name], one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Kaṅkola, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Virāṭ, the meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to the deity Ucchiṣṭagaṇapati, on the heart. Then: "Salutation to Hasti-hṛdaya (the Elephant-heart), on the hands; *svāhā* to Piśāci-śiras (the Piśāci-head), on the head; *vaṣaṭ* to Likhā-śikhā (the Likhā-crest), on the crest; *huṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*); and the weapon (*astra*) is declared by the entire mantra. Thus the procedure for the five limbs (*pañcāṅga*) is described. As for the meditation (*dhyāna*), it is as previously stated for the six-syllabled *Vakratuṇḍa* mantra. Now..."

The variations of this very mantra are as follows: *Oṃ krāṃ krīṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ huṃ cce cce phaṭ svāhā*. This mantra consists of eleven syllables. Its seer (*ṛṣi*) and other attributes have been previously stated; its meditation (*dhyāna*) and so forth are like those of the six-syllabled Vakratuṇḍa mantra. *Ekadaṃṣṭrāya hastimukhāya lambodarāya ucchiṣṭātmane kroṃ bluṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ cce ccesvāhā*. This mantra consists of nineteen syllables. Its seer, meditation, and other attributes are like those of the six-syllabled Vakratuṇḍa mantra. *Oṃ namo bhagavate ekadaṃṣṭrāya hastimukhāya*.

*Laṃvodarāyocchiṣṭāya mahātmane kroṃ blūṃ hrīṃ huṃ cce ce svāhā*. This mantra consists of thirty-eight syllables. The seer (*ṛṣi*) and other details have been stated previously; the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) is proclaimed with the six seed-syllables (*bīja*). As for the meditation (*dhyāna*), it is exactly like that of the previously mentioned Vakratuṇḍa Yakṣara mantra. Regarding "with the six seed-syllables": *krauṃ* is the heart, *blūṃ* is the head, *hrīṃ* is the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *huṃ* is the armor (*kavaca*), *cce* is the eye, and *cce* is the weapon (*astra*). These are the four mantras of Ucchiṣṭagaṇeśa. [Thus ends the work of Gausvāmijanārdanabhaṭṭa, son of Gausvāmijagannivāsa.]

[Thus ends the first chapter in the *Mantracandrikā* composed by Viracita. (1) Thus concludes the section on the Gaṇapati-mantras. Now, the Śakti-mantras: therein, first, the Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the mantra consisting of the collection of fifty-one phonemes from the letter 'A' to the letter 'Kṣa'. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with that very [mantra], one should perform the assignment of limbs (*nyāsa*): "Salutation to Brahmā, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chaṃdas*), on the mouth; salutation to the Goddess Śrī-Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart; salutation to the Seeds (*vīja*) which are the consonants (*hal*), on the private parts; [salutation to the Powers (*śakti*) which are the vowels (*svara*), on the feet]."

"Obeisance to *yoḥ* from the vowels and the *Śaktis*; obeisance to the manifest *Kīlaka* in the navel. Having thus spoken with palms joined, this is the application (*viniyoga*) for the *Mātṛkā-nyāsa*. Then, having placed the mantras on both hands from the thumbs to the palms—*aṃ kaṃ (4) āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *iṃ caṃ (4) īṃ śirase svāhā*, *oṃ ṭaṃ (4) oṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *eṃ taṃ (4) kavacāya huṃ*, *oṃ paṃ (4) oṃ netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*, *ayaṃ raṃ (0) astrāya phaṭ*—one should likewise place them on the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), beginning with the heart.

One should meditate upon the Goddess seated on a lotus throne, her head adorned with the crescent moon, possessing three eyes, and having a body of fifty syllables [in sequence]. She is as radiant as the autumnal moon and the *kuṇḍala* (ear-ornament), bent by the weight of her breasts, and holding in her lotus-like hands a vessel of nectar (*dāna*), a rosary (*akṣavatī*), a beautiful jar shining with the essence of nectar, and an auspicious book. The meditation on the weapons begins from the lower right hand and ends with the lower left hand: [the first hand holds] the vessel of nectar (*dāna*), [and the others hold] the boon-granting gesture (*vara*). Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) upon the recitation, one should offer the oblation.

One should bow to Mārīcī. This is the *Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī* or *Vāgvādinī* mantra: *vada vada vāgvādini svāhā*. Having performed three breath-restraints (*prāṇāyāma*) with this ten-syllable mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the sage Gaṇeśa on the head; salutation to the Virāṭ meter in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Sarasvatī in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllables (hal) in the secret place; salutation to the powers (khara) in the feet; salutation to the pin (kīlaka), which is the Manifest (Vyakti), in the navel. [This is done] for the sake of accomplishing all my desired goals.

Having spoken thus with palms joined in *añjali*, one should perform the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual as previously described for the Mothers, beginning with "Aṃ Aṃ Hṛdayāya Namaḥ," or alternatively:
"Hrāṃ Vāk Ṛgveda-hṛdayāya Namaḥ; Hrīṃ Vāk Yajurveda-śirase Svāhā; Hūṃ Vāk Sāmaveda-śikhāyai Vaṣaṭ; Hraiṃ Vāk Atharvaveda-kavacāya Huṃ Svāhā;
Ṣaḍaṅga-netrāya Vauṣaṭ; Hraḥ. Having uttered the entire mantra, [one should worship] those who dwell in the Purāṇas, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, Dharmaśāstra, Itihāsa, and Kalpa.

Having performed the *ṣaḍaṅga* ritual with the mantras "thānārāśaṃsī astrāya phaṭ" by placing them on the hands from the thumbs to the palms, and having likewise placed them on the heart and other centers, one should meditate as follows: "May the Goddess of Speech (Sarasvatī) be ever for our prosperity—she who rests upon a white lotus as bright as a jasmine flower, whose head is adorned with the moon, who holds a pen and the Vidyā-mantra in her two lotus-like hands, and whose slender form is bent by the weight of her breasts. Having meditated thus—with the pen in the right hand and the book in the left—one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity. After the recitation...

Having performed that *ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* with the *ta-raṃ-kara-ṣa* syllables, and having offered the recitation (*japa*) to the deity, one should prostrate. This is the mantra of Vāgvādinī. Now, the mantra of Haṃsavāgīśvarī: *hreṃ hrīṃ yeṃ hrīṃ oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this eleven-syllable mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Śakti, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chaṃdas*), on the mouth;

salutation to Haṃsavāgīśvarī, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart. Then, with palms joined in reverence, one should state: "This is for the attainment of all my desired goals—this is the application (*viniyoga*)."

Having performed the *ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* (assignment of the six limbs) as follows: *Aiṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *Aiṃ śirase svāhā*, *Aiṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *Aiṃ kavacāya huṃ*, *Aiṃ netrāya vauṣaṭ*, *Aiṃ astrāya phaṭ*;

and having assigned the mantras thus: *Oṃ namaḥ* at the *brahmarandhra*, *Hrīṃ* between the eyebrows, *Aiṃ* in the right eye, *Hrīṃ* in the left eye, *Oṃ* in the right ear, *Saṃ* in the left ear, *Raṃ* in the right nostril, *Svaṃ* in the left nostril, *Tyaiḥ* on the face, and *Liṅgenaṃ pāyaumaḥ* [on the private parts], one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: One should meditate upon that goddess of speech (*Vāgdevatā*), who is stainless...

One should meditate upon her, seated upon a swan from Malaya and other such mounts, her radiant bodily luster shining with the laughter of a multitude of camphor, kunda flowers, and jasmine; she has a face like the full moon that kisses the crescent moon, a gentle smile, and a dark complexion; she holds in her lotus-hands the *vidyā-vīṇā*, a water-pot, and a rosary of beads, which shine like a jar rising from the ocean. Regarding the visualization of the weapons: "The first [weapon] is in the two upper hands starting from the left, and the others are in the two lower hands starting from the right. Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, after the recitation, one should again perform the *kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* and offer the recitation.
One should prostrate after offering the *vyasta-samarpaṇa*. This is the mantra of Haṃsa-Vāgīśvarī. Now, for the second [form], Haṃsa-Vāgīśvarī: *Aiṃ namo bhagavati vada vada vāgdevi svāhā*.

Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this sixteen-syllable mantra, and having assigned the source (*ṛṣi*), meter (*chandas*), and deity (*devatā*) as previously stated for Haṃsa-Vāgīśvarī, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Aiṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *Śirase svāhā*, *Bhagavati śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *Vada vada kavacāya huṃ*, *Vāgdevi netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*, *Svāhā astrāya*.

Having performed the *ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* with the mantra *yaphaṭ iti*, one should meditate as follows: She possesses the luster of a jasmine flower or the moon, wears white garments, and is adorned with white garlands and unguents. She holds in her lotus-like hands the *Vyākhyā* (Exposition) [mudrā], the *Vidyā* [mudrā], the vessel of nectar (*amṛtakalaśa*), and a rosary of beads (*varṇamālā*). She stands upon a white lotus, her head is radiant with the crescent moon, she is endowed with three eyes, and she is bowed by her full breasts for the sake of our prosperity. Beginning from the upper right hand and ending with the lower right hand, one should meditate on the weapons: the *Vyākhyā* [mudrā] is the *Vyākhyāna-mudrā*. Having thus meditated according to the [tradition]...
Having offered the *kṛtikā-japa* to the Goddess and bowed down like a serpent, this concludes the second mantra of Haṃsa-Vāgīśvarī. Alternatively, regarding the two mantras of Vāgvādinī:

having performed three rounds of *prāṇāyāma* with the eleven-syllable mantra, "Aiṃ vācaspataye amṛte klavaḥ su" (Aiṃ vācaspataye amṛte klavaḥ su), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the Ṛṣis and other elements as follows: "Oṃ, obeisance to Śakti, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; obeisance to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chandas*), in the mouth; obeisance to the Goddess Śrī-Vāgīśvarī, the Deity (*devatā*), in the heart. Then, [perform the limb-nyāsa]: "Aiṃ, obeisance to the Heart; vācaspataye, svāhā to the Head; amṛte, vaṣaṭ to the Crest-lock (*śikhā*)."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Pluvaḥ kavacāya huṃ plūḥ" for the armor and "Astrāya phaṭ" for the weapon, and having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) on both hands with the root mantra, one should place the mantras from the heart to the weapon upon the five fingers—starting from the thumb to the little finger—conjoined with their respective seed-syllables (*jāti*), excluding the eyes: "Hṛdayāya namaḥ," "Śirase svāhā," and so forth. Having thus placed them on the five limbs starting from the heart, excluding the eyes, one should meditate as follows: [She] is seated upon a lotus, holding a pair of lotuses and a book in her lotus-hands; she has a moon upon her crown, an eye in her forehead, the luster of pearls, and breasts that are bowed down.

Worship Vāgdevī, who is served by the lords of sages and bestows poetic genius; perform meditation on her weapons starting from the upper left hand and ending with the lower left hand. Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having again performed the *karāṅganyāsa* (assignment of hands and limbs), one should offer the recitation to the Goddess and prostrate. This is the first mantra of Vāgvādinī. Now, the second mantra:

having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the three-syllable mantra "Cāṃ Rūṃ Svāṃ," one should assign the *ṛṣi*, *chandas*, and other attributes as in the previously mentioned ten-syllable mantra of Vāgvādinī.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the six limbs, beginning with the heart, using the syllables joined with the seed-mantras and the *jātis*—namely, *syāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *ruṃ śirase svāhā*, *svoṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *vāṃ kavacāya huṃ*, *rūṃ netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*, and *svoṃ astrāya phaṭ*—one should meditate as follows: May she, whose body shines with a pearl necklace, whose beautiful crest-jewel is adorned by the digit of power (*śakti-kalā*), who holds in her hands a book, a rosary, a water-pot, and the goddess of learning (*Vidyā*), whose slender waist is bent by the weight of her two full, high breasts, and who sits upon a white lotus; may she, who is ever saluted by the three worlds, be for our speech.

The visualization of the weapons (*āyudha-dhyāna*) is as follows: the first [hand] on the upper and lower right arms holds the *dhī* (wisdom) and the *śrī* (fortune); the other two, on the upper and lower left hands, hold the remaining [weapons]. Having performed the visualization and recitation (*dhyāna-japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsa*), one should offer the recitation to the Goddess and prostrate. Some say the mantra is *Vāk-rūsvoṃ*; others say that in place of *vāk*, the seed-syllable (*vāk-bīja*) should be used. Therefore, the recitation and so forth should be performed here according to the instruction of one’s Guru. This is the second mantra, [that of] Vāgvādinī. Now, [the mantra of] Pārijāta-Sarasvatī.

The mantra is: *Oṃ hrīṃ hsaiṃ hrīṃ oṃ sasvatyai namaḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this eleven-syllable mantra, one should perform the visualization of the seer (*ṛṣi*), the recitation (*japa*), and so forth, as previously described for Haṃsavāgīśvarī. This concludes Pārijātasarasvatī. Now, the mantra of Saptakoṭīśvarī: *Kaḥ saḥ caṇḍike saḥ kaḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control with this seven-syllable mantra, [one should assign: *Namaḥ* to Brahmā, the seer, on the head; to Gāyatrī, the meter, in the mouth; and to the deity Saptakoṭīśvarī in the heart.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the limbs on the hands with the mantra beginning with *yainamiti* and *cāñcīmiti*, one should meditate upon her as [one does] Tripurā. Her visualization will be described later.

Having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having again performed the six-limbed placement (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) and so forth, one should offer the recitation to the Goddess and prostrate. This is the mantra of Saptakoṭīśvarī. Now follows another mantra, that of Vāgvādinī:
*oṃ vadavada vāgvādinī hrīṃ klīṃ klinne kledini mahākṣobhaṃ kuru sauḥ mokṣaṃ kuruṣva oṃ*. Thus ends the twenty-ninth [chapter].

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas* with the mantra consisting of the syllable *dakṣara*, one should arrange everything for this [mantra] just as was done for the previously mentioned *Vāgvādinī*. There is a nine-syllabled mantra beginning with *praṇava* (oṃ) and ending with *vāgvādinī*;
another is thirteen syllables long, including the months and so forth; and another is seven syllables long, beginning with *bālā* and ending with *praṇava*. This mantra consists of three parts.

The specific purpose of these individual components is stated in the *Śrīśivārcanacandrikā*. Thus ends the *Vāgvādinī* mantra. In this way, the four mantras have been combined. *Vāgvā*... [text truncated]

The Bālāmantra for worldly purposes is as follows: *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this three-syllabled mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): "Salutation to the Seer Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti on the head; salutation to the Paṅkti metre on the mouth; salutation to the Deity Śrī Bālā on the heart; salutation to the Seed-syllable *Aiṃ* on the private parts; salutation to the Power (*Śakti*) *Sauḥ* on the feet; salutation to the Pin (*Kīlaka*) *Klīṃ* on the navel. Having thus performed the placement, one should say with palms joined in reverence: "This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the attainment of my fourfold aims of human existence (*caturvidha-puruṣārtha*). Then, [recite]: *Aiṃ* salutation to the Heart; *Klīṃ*...
Having performed the assignment (*nyāsa*) of the six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*)— *śirase svāhā*, *sauḥ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *aiṃ kavacāya huṃ*, *klīṃ netrāya vauṣaṭ*, *sauḥ astrāya phaṭ*—

upon the hands from the thumb to the little finger, and having likewise assigned them to the six limbs starting with the heart, one should perform meditation as follows: [She who is] dark blue like a wandering bee, with a braid of hair adorned with pure flowers,
shining with a streak of split pearls throbbing at the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*), her forehead slightly curved by a dangling pearl-streak, [and] possessing pure pearls and diamonds...

She wears a crown of crescent moons; her three eyes, dark as wandering bees, surpass the brilliance of the sun; she is adorned with great jeweled earrings shining like the sun; she is decorated with necklaces of pearls sparkling like the planet Venus; she shines with the radiant luster of neck-chains, armlets, and rows of leaf-shaped ornaments; she is clothed in garments as white as the waves of the Ganges and camphor; her arms and chest are resplendent like beautiful sandalwood vines; she possesses the brilliant glow of clusters of gems from her bracelets and other fine ornaments; and her hands are like delicate sprouts of coral.

One should meditate upon the goddess Vāśī, who bestows subjugation, good fortune, and eloquence; she is adorned with a girdle of vajras, lapis lazuli, and strings of pearls, and possesses a stainless radiance. Her lotus-feet are graced by the shape of red lotus petals, and she is embellished with pearl necklaces resembling a garland of stars. O lady of beautiful countenance, one should contemplate her holding a book in one left hand and granting fearlessness to the practitioner with the other; with her two right hands, she holds a rosary and bestows boons. One’s beloved should remember her as being white as a jar of milk and full of splendor.

Having meditated on the visualization of the weapons as described for the right and left upper [hands] and so forth, and having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should again perform the *kara-ṣaḍaṅga* (hand and six-limbed ritual) immediately after the recitation.

Then, having offered the recitation to the Goddess with the previously mentioned mantra, "O most secret of secrets... and so forth, one should bow to the deity. This is the *Bālā-mantra*. Now, the *Bhairavī-mantra*: *Hli Hsklīṃ Hsrauṃḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this three-syllable mantra, one should assign: "Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), upon the head; salutation to Paṅkti, the Metre (*chandas*), upon the mouth."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "to the deity Śrī Tripurabhairavī, *namas*" at the heart, and having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) starting with *hsraṃ hsrīṃ* and so forth, one should meditate [on her] as [described for] Tripurā. Alternatively, one should meditate on her residing in the center of the pericarp of a red lotus situated in the heart— red like a hibiscus flower, wearing red garments and ornaments, with great delusion washed away by her smile, three-eyed, moon-crested, the embodiment of the ocean of the birth of all the essence of universal beauty, and her limbs adorned by those known as Brahmā, Aghora, Netra, Rudreśa, Śiva, and Muṇḍa.

One should meditate upon Tripurabhairavī—the Great Goddess, holding a rosary of pearls and a book in her hands, bestowing the gestures of granting boons (*varada*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*), sweet with bliss, her eyes rolling with intoxication, beautiful with red unguents on her limbs. Regarding the visualization of the weapons: the first two are in the upper right and left hands, while the others are in the lower right and left hands. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, after the recitation, one should again perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), offer the recitation to the Goddess, and prostrate. There are indeed many other variations of this very mantra.

The separate meditations and other practices involving the seed-syllables (vījas) such as *gbh* and others are all to be sought in our grandfather’s work, the *Śivārcanacandrikā*; for fear of excessive length, we have not written them here. This concludes the *Bhairavī-mantra*. Alternatively, having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the five-syllable mantra *vāṇeśvarī drīṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ*, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows:
"Salutation to Madana, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the meter (*chaṃdas*), on the mouth; salutation to the deity Vāṇeśvarī on the heart. Then, [reciting] *drāṃ*...

"Hṛdayāya namaḥ, drīṃ śirase svāhā, klīṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ, chūṃ kavacāya huṃ, saḥ netrāya vauṣaṭ, samasta-mantra-aṅga-astre phaṭ. Having thus assigned the six limb-mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) to the hands, beginning from the thumb and ending with the little finger, and having also assigned them to the six limbs starting from the heart, one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "She who has the splendor of the rising sun, adorned with various ornaments, whose garments and body are red like the *bandhūka* flower, and whose two arms shine with a sugarcane bow and flowery arrows."

Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having again performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should offer the recitation to the Goddess and prostrate. This is the mantra of Pañcākāmeśvarī.

Now, the mantras of Rājamātaṅgī: *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ namo bhagavati śrīmātaṅgeśvari sarvajanamanohari sarvamukharāji sarvamukharañjani sarvarāja-vaśaṅkari sarvastrīpuruṣavaśaṅkari sarvaduṣṭamṛgavaśaṅkari sarvalokam amukaṃ me vaśam ānaya svāhā*.

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas* with this mantra of eighty-eight syllables, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Oṃ, salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chandas*), on the face; salutation to the Goddess Śrīmātaṅgeśvarī, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart. Then, with palms joined in reverence, one should say: "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of all my desired goals. Following this, [one recites]: "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, Śrīmātaṅgeśvarī, who captivates the minds of all people, salutation to the Heart; salutation to the Head, which colors the faces of all."

*svāhā sarvarājavaśāṅkarī-sarvastrīpuruṣavaśaṅkari-śikhāyai vaṭ*, *sarvaduṣṭamṛgavaśaṅkari-sarvasattvavaśaṅkarī-vacāyai huṃ*, *sarvalokam amukaṃ me vaśam ānaya netratrayāya vauṣaṭ svāhā astrāya phaṭ*. Having thus assigned these six limb-mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) to the two hands, from the thumbs to the palms, and having also assigned them to the six limbs beginning with the heart, one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "In the midst of the ocean of nectar, upon a delightful jewel-island, [is] a golden enclosure..."

In a pavilion constructed of jewels, adorned with *kadaṃba*, *bilva*, *kadamba*, and *ekaḥnya* trees, and graced by a maṇḍapa draped in fine cloth—there, in the center of an altar, upon an auspicious jewel-throne spread with divine coverings, there is a great eight-petaled lotus, rich with filaments and a beautiful pericarp. In its center is a triangle; outside that is another eight-petaled lotus; further out, there should be a sixteen-petaled one;

and on the exterior, a four-petaled one. This supreme maṇḍala is inscribed with the four-armed [diagram] and possesses four gates. In its center, seated comfortably, is the dark-hued [deity] with a pure smile, [seated upon] a *kadaṃba*...

Adorned with garlands and ornaments, worshipped by gods and asuras, she possesses long, flowing locks and has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament. Her forehead is marked with a tilaka, and her face is slightly smiling. She is somewhat youthful, radiant with a beautiful forehead, and possesses waves of folds upon her waist, graced by a line of fine body hair.
She is endowed with every ornament, embellished with necklaces, and decorated with waist-bands bound with clusters of various gems, as well as bracelets inlaid with jewels and camphor.

One should meditate upon Mātaṅgī, adorned with armlets and jewels, her two arms graced by the brilliance of various clusters of gems; a young woman whose eyes roll with intoxication, whose full and rounded breasts rise high;
resplendent with long pendants and earrings hanging from her ears; a youthful maiden dark as the Tamāla tree, possessing a honeyed voice and the form of the sixty-four arts;
with parrots and sarika birds at her side; resembling ten million rising suns or like the Japā flower; or likewise, one may meditate on her as being yellow in complexion.

Having meditated upon Nīṃparā and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and after the recitation, having again performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should offer the recitation to the Goddess with the mantra "Guhyātiguhyam" and bow to the Goddess and the Guru. This is the Rājamātaṅgī mantra. Now, another Rājamātaṅgī mantra: Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Ai Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ Namaḥ Bhagavati Śrīmātaṅgeśvari Sarvajana-manohari Sarvamukha-rañjani Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sarvarāja-vaśaṅkari Sarvastri-puruṣa-vaśaṅkari Sarvadu... [text truncated]

Having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma) with this mantra consisting of ninety-eight syllables: *ṣṭamṛgavaśaṃkarisarvasatvavaśaṃkarisarvalokavaśaṃkariamukaṃmevaśamānayasvāhā śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ sauṃḥ klīṃ aiṃ*, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to Śrīmātangaśvarī, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart. Then, with palms joined in reverence, one should say: "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of all my desired goals," and [recite] *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sarvajanama...* [etc.].

"Oṃ namo nāharihṛdayāya svāhā; oṃ sarvamukharañjanīśirase svāhā; oṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sarvarājavaśaṅkari śikhāyai vaṣaṭ (2); sarvastripuruṣavaśaṅkari kavacāya huṃ; sarvaduṣṭamṛgavaśaṅkari netratrayāya vauṣaṭ (3); sarvasattvavaśaṅkari astrāya phaṭ.

Having thus performed the assignment of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the hands and the heart and other parts, one should perform meditation. Alternatively, having performed the six-limbed ritual using the seed-syllable of desire (*kāma-bīja*)—*klāṃ klīṃ*—endowed with the six long vowels, one should meditate.

Just as [she was seen] in the middle of a jewel-island within the great ocean of nectar, in a forest of wish-fulfilling trees, in the center of a jeweled pavilion, upon a jeweled lion-throne— Mātaṅgī,

delighted by drinking the flood of honey, her eyes rolling with intoxication, her face perspiring, her beautiful braid shimmering like a *kadamba* flower, her hand radiant with a lute, wearing crimson garments, her lips like the bimba fruit, marked with musk tilaka, her crown like the moon, her ears adorned with conch earrings, and her belly slightly curved.

One should meditate with joy upon her who is adorned with a golden girdle, waist-cloth, dark-blue garments, necklaces, armlets, beautiful neck-ornaments, and anklets; who, with a glance equal to a gracious smile, gratifies her devotees;

and likewise, one should contemplate Śuka standing at her side, the embodiment of all arts. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*), and having again performed the *ṣaḍaṅga* ritual, one should offer the recitation to the Goddess and prostrate. This is the second mantra. Now follows the third mantra, the Rājamātaṅgī-mantra: "O supreme one among the eighty-eight previously extracted [mantras], bring all beings under control..."

Immediately after the *karīti* mantra, one should append the seven syllables "sa rājya lakṣmī prade," and then say "sarvalokam amukaṃ" and so forth; thus, it becomes ninety-five syllables. The *ṛṣi* and other details are as previously stated. For the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) mantras, such as "Āṃ hṛdayāya," "Īṃ śirase," and so on, the visualization (*dhyāna*) is the same as that of the previously mentioned mantra. This is the third [mantra]. Now follows the fourth: the Rājamātaṅgī mantra: Oṃ hrīṃ namo brahmaśrī rājite rājapūjite jape vijaye gaurī gāndhārī bhuvanaśaṅkarī sarvastrīpuruṣa...

Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the fifty-four-syllable mantra: *vaśaṃkarisusudududyedyaivāvāhrīṃ svāhā*, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other components as follows: "Salutation to Aja, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; salutation to Nivṛt-Gāyatrī, the meter, on the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Rājamātaṅgī, on the heart. Then, having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) beginning with *hrīṃ hrīṃ*, one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as previously described for the mantra. At the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), having again performed the six-limbed ritual and offered the recitation to the Goddess, one should prostrate. Thus ends the fourth [chapter].

Now, the fifth mantra: therein, from the previously mentioned forty-five-syllable mantra, one should state the phrase "the subduer of the three worlds" (*tribhuvanavaśaṃkarī*), followed by the phrase "the subduer of all the worlds" (*sarvalokavaśaṃkarī*), and then say "all women and men," etc., ending with *svāhā*. One should omit the initial *praṇava* (oṃ). Thus, the mantra consists of sixty-one syllables. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the assignment of the seer and other elements (*ṛṣyādi*) as follows: "Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Seer, on the head; salutation to Nivṛt-Gāyatrī, the Metre, on the mouth; salutation to the Goddess Śrī-Gaurī, the Deity, on the heart. This is the procedure for the seer and other elements.

Having performed the assignment of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the hands, heart, and other parts with the mantra: *Hrīṃ namo brahma-śrī-rājite rāja-pūjite hṛdayāya namaḥ; Jape vijaye gaurī-gāndhārī śirase svāhā; Tribhuvana-śaṅkari śikhāyai vaṣaṭ; Sarva-strī-puruṣa-vaśaṅkari netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ; Su-su-du-du-ye-ye-vā-vā-hrīṃ svāhā astrāya phaṭ*, one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: [She who has] a crown made of the rising moon, whose lotus-like hands are beautiful with the [noose and] goad, and who is the color of the bandhujīva flower...
"May this Pārvatī—whose body is adorned with the red rays of her eyes which are like the lotuses of the multitude of gods, and who is endowed with garments and flowers—be our prosperity.

Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's ability, and having again performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) at the end of the recitation, one should offer [the merit] and prostrate. This is the fifth mantra. Now follows the sixth, the Rājamātaṅgī mantra:
*Oṃ rājamukhi rājābhimukhi vaśyamukhi hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ devadevi mahādevi devādhidevi sarvajanasya mukhaṃ mama vaśaṃ kuru kuru svāhā*.

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas* with the mantra consisting of seventy-three syllables, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the Ṛṣis and other limbs as follows: "Oṃ, salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to the Goddess Śrīmātaṅgeśvarī, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart. Then, [one should recite]: "Oṃ rājamukhi rājābhimukhi, salutation to the Heart (*hṛdaya*); vaśyamukhi hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ, svāhā to the Head (*śiras*); devi devi, vaṣaṭ to the Crest-lock (*śikhā*); mahādevi, huṃ to the Armor (*kavaca*); devādhidevi, vauṣaṭ to the Eyes (*netra*); [sarvajana...]"

*Syāmukhaṃ mama vaśaṃ kuru kuru svāhā astrāya phaṭ*. Having thus performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the hands and heart, meditating as before, and at the end of the recitation having again performed the six-limbed ritual and offered the recitation to the Goddess, one should prostrate. This is the sixth mantra. Now the seventh: *Hrīṃ namo hili hili vaḍanā taṃgini svāhā*. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) over these fifteen syllables, one should perform the [recitation of] the seer (*ṛṣi*), meditation (*dhyāna*), the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), and so forth, as before. This is the seventh mantra. Now the eighth: *Aiṃ namaḥ śrīmātaṃ...* (The text continues with the name of the goddess).

"O you who speak unfailing truth, descend, descend into my ear; speak the truth, speak! Obeisance to the glorious Mātaṅgī, come hither!"—having performed three breath-restraints (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra consisting of forty-four syllables, one should perform the visualization of the *ṛṣi*, the recitation (*japa*), and so forth, as previously described. This is the eighth [section]. Now, "Obeisance! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O Mistress of the Mātaṅgas, you who bring all under control, svāhā!"—having performed three breath-restraints with this twenty-three-syllable mantra, [one should place it] on the head.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), at the mouth; salutation to the *Ṛgveda-Gāyatrī* metre at the face; salutation to the deity Śrīmātaṅgeśvarī at the heart," one should then perform the placement on the hands, heart, and other limbs with: *Aiṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *Klīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *Sauḥ* to the crest-lock, *vaṣaṭ*; *Aiṃ* to the armor, *huṃ*; *Klīṃ* to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *Sauḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*. Having performed this, one should carry out all subsequent rites, such as meditation (*dhyāna*), as previously described. This is the ninth [mantra]. Now, the tenth mantra: *Kāma-nirañjani svāhā*.

Having performed three breath-control exercises (*prāṇāyāma*) with the six-syllable mantra, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other components as follows: "Salutation to Saṃmohana, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; salutation to Nivṛt, the *chandas*, on the mouth; salutation to the deity Sarvasaṃmohinī on the heart. Then, having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands, heart, and so forth, using the mantras: "O Kāminī, to the heart, *raṃjani*, *svāhā* for the head; *kāminī*, to the tuft (*śikhā*), *huṃ*; O Kāminī, to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*; *raṃjani*, to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *svāhā*, to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*," one should meditate as follows: "She who has dark limbs, holding a lute in her two arms..."

Having meditated thus: "She who moves about, beautifully adorned, with a fierce crest-ornament, deluding the world with various songs," and having completed the recitation (*japa*), one should again perform the six-limbed rite (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and offer the recitation to the Goddess. Then, this is the eleventh mantra: *Nama ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālīmātaṅgi sarvavaśaṅkari svāhā*. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with this nineteen-syllable mantra, one should perform the Nyāsa: "Salutation to Tuṃburu Nārada together with his Śakti on the head; salutation to the Nivṛtt-Gāyatrī metre on the mouth; [salutation] to Śrī Mātaṅgī on the heart..."

"Obeisance to the goddess Geśvarī; this is the application for the attainment of my desired goal. Having said this, one should perform the assignment of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) as follows: "Obeisance to the heart," "Ucchiṣṭa to the head," "Caṇḍālī to the crest-lock (*śikhā*)," "Mātaṅgī to the armor (*kavaca*)," "Hūṃ, O you who bring all under control, to the eyes, vauṣaṭ svāhā," and "Phaṭ to the weapon (*astra*). Then, the meditation (*dhyāna*): [I meditate upon] Mātaṅgī, whose feet are moist with fresh lac-dye, who is dark-complexioned and dressed in black silk, holding a lute and a fly-whisk, her breasts full, adorned with pearl and coral ornaments, beautiful-limbed, wearing white conch-shell earrings, and possessing lips like the bimba fruit.

One should meditate upon her who has a smile on her lips, whose braided hair is adorned with *alaka* curls, who has lotus-like eyes, and who is dark like a blue lotus (*indīvara*). Having thus meditated, at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), offer the recitation, and prostrate.

Regarding the variations of this very mantra, he says: one begins with *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, another with *klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, and yet another with *klīṃ*. Among these, for the first mantra, one should place "Salutation to the sage Nārada, the son of Tuṃburu" upon the head; for the other two verses, "Salutation to the sage Madana. [The rest of] the six-limbed ritual, meditation, and so forth, is the same for all.

This should be understood as being like the mantra of nineteen syllables; this is the eleventh mantra. Now, the twelfth mantra: *Aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ namaḥ ucchiṣṭacaṇḍāli mātaṅgi sarvavaśaṃkari svāhā sauḥ klīṃ aiṃ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this twenty-five-syllable mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the sage Dakṣiṇāmūrti on the head; salutation to the Nivṛt-Gāyatrī meter in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī in the heart. Then, one should state the application: "For the attainment of my desired goal."

Having uttered "Gaḥ" with palms joined in reverence, one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as follows: "Aiṃ namo mahādayāya namaḥ," "Klīṃ ucchiṣṭa-śirase svāhā," "Sauḥ caṇḍāli śikhāyai vaṣaṭ," "Aiṃ mātaṅgikavacāya huṃ," "Klīṃ sarvavaśaṅkari netrāya vauṣaṭ," and "Sauḥ svāhā astrāya phaṭ. Having performed this, one should meditate [on her] thus: "She who has a braid upon her shoulder, a crest of gathered flowers, and a dark top-knot; adorned with pearls, possessing full breasts, playing the lute (*vallakī*); intoxicated by honey-wine, speaking sweet words, and dark-complexioned."

"I constantly meditate upon Mātaṅgī, whose limbs are delicate and who bestows all fruits. Having thus meditated, performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) at the end of the recitation (*japa*), and offered the merit, one should prostrate. Thus ends the twelfth [chapter].
[Thus ends the second illumination in the *Mantracandrikā* composed by Gosvāmin Janārdana Bhaṭṭa, son of Gosvāmin Jagannivāsa.

Now, the mantras of Bhuvaneśvarī: having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the single-syllable mantra *hrīṃ*, one should say: "Salutation to Śakti, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the meter (*chandas*), on the mouth."

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to the deity Śrībhuvaneśvarī in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *haṃ* in the secret place; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *īṃ* in the two feet; salutation to the pin (*kīlaka*) *rakī* in the navel," and having declared with palms joined, "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of attaining the fourfold aims of human life (*puruṣārtha*"), and having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) beginning with *hrīṃ hrīṃ* and so forth, one should meditate: "She who possesses the luster of the rising sun, who has the cool-rayed moon as her crest-ornament, who sits upon a lotus throne, who is three-eyed, whose four arms are adorned with the noose, the goad, the boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness, and whose face shines with a gentle smile."

One should meditate upon the Goddess, whose creeper-like limbs are bent by the weight of her breasts, visualizing the weapons starting from the upper left hand down to the lower left hand. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having performed the *ṣaḍaṅga* ritual on the hands at the conclusion, one should offer the recitation to the Goddess and prostrate. This is the first mantra. Now the second: having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the three-syllable mantra "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ," and having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other elements as before, one performs the *ṣaḍaṅga* ritual as follows: "Aiṃ Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart; Aiṃ Hrīṃ, to the head; Rāṃ Huṃ," and so forth.

Having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) for the long-lived one, one should meditate [on the Goddess] who has the luster of the *bandhūka* flower, possesses three eyes, is adorned with a crescent moon shining like ten million moons, and holds in her two hands a vessel of jewels filled with various gems. One should meditate on the gentle Goddess, whose moon-like face is smiling, who has large breasts, and whose left foot shines from a jewel-pitcher at her heart. Regarding the visualization of the weapons: she holds a jewel-vessel in her left hand and a lotus in her right. (This is the reading found in the *Vidyārṇava* and the *Śivārcanacandrikā*). One should always meditate on her as being endowed with the *varābhīti* (boon-granting and fear-dispelling) gestures and the noose (*pāśa*) and goad (*aṅkuśa*). Having thus meditated...

At the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the hands and having offered the recitation to the Goddess, one should prostrate. This is the second [method]. Now, the third: having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the three-syllable mantra *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ*, and having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the limbs starting with the head as in the case of the single-syllable [mantra], one should perform the six-limbed ritual on the hands, heart, and so forth, with: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Hṛdayāya Namaḥ*, *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Śirase Svāhā*, and so on; then one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*): "Her form shines like the ocean, she has three eyes glowing, and her yellow breasts..."

I meditate upon the radiant Ambikā within my own heart—she who carries in her lotus-hands the gestures of granting boons (*vara*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*) along with jeweled vessels; she who eternally rests upon a red lotus, whose crown shines with the cool-rayed moon, who is adorned with necklaces and ornaments, and whose feet are worshipped by the Lord of the Universe. This is the visualization of the weapons, beginning from the lower right hand and ending with the lower left hand.

Having thus meditated, at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) on the hands, offer the recitation to the Goddess, and prostrate. Now follows the fourth mantra of Bhuvaneśvarī: *Ā Hrīṃ Kroṃ*, which consists of three syllables.

Having performed three rounds of *prāṇāyāma* with the *Rama-mantra*, having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the limbs starting from the head as in the one-syllable mantra, and having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *hrāṃ hrīm* and so forth, one should meditate: "One should remember the Supreme Bhuvaneśvarī in the heart, seated upon a lotus, holding a goad, a boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness in Her hands, Her body possessing the splendor of a multitude of rising suns.

Having meditated on the weapons—[the goad] in the right upper hand, [the boon-granting gesture] in the lower right hand, and the others in the left hands—one should perform the *ṛṣi*-placement and so forth at the end of the recitation, offer the recitation, and prostrate. Thus ends the fourth [chapter].

Now, the mantras of Durgā: having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the eight-syllable mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ durgāyai namaḥ," one should perform the placement of the Ṛṣi and other elements as follows: "Oṃ, salutation to Nārada, the Seer, at the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Meter, in the mouth; salutation to Śrī Durgā, the Deity, in the heart. Having thus performed the placement of the Ṛṣi and others, the application is stated as: "For the attainment of all my desires, this is the yoga. Then: "Oṃ hrīṃ durgāyai hrāṃ, salutation to the Heart; Oṃ hrīṃ durgāyai hrīṃ, svāhā to the Head; Oṃ hrīṃ durgāyai hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the Crest-lock (*śikhā*)," and so forth.

Having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) of the Sun, one should meditate upon Durgā, who sits upon a lion-throne, possesses the luster of emerald, wears the crescent moon on her crest, and holds a conch, a discus, a lotus, and a sword in her palms; she is adorned with three eyes, shines brightly, destroys fear and suffering, and her limbs are decorated with jeweled ornaments.
