*Hrīṃ aiṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa nirantarakrīḍāsakta śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ śirase svāhā*. *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kṛṣṇāya pramuditacetase śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*. (3) *Nityapriyāya* (3) *kavacāya huṃ*. (3) *Klīṃ netrāya vauṣaṭ*. (3) *Gopījanavallabhāya svāhā*. (3) *Astrāya phaṭ*.

Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of these mantras from the thumbs to the palms of both hands, and also having performed the placement on the six limbs beginning with the heart, one should perform meditation as follows: In my own charming and supreme city...

It was situated entirely within the midst of the ocean, possessing vast, lofty, and great fortresses with gate-towers and excellent streets; it was crowded with networks of palaces washed with white plaster and raised high like clouds, adorned with red mansions and expansive doorways with leaf-like panels; it was filled with the finest dwellings of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras, as well as the houses of various artisans and the stables for elephants, horses, camels, and donkeys;
it was joined by countless houses for cattle, goats, buffaloes, and the like, and gathered together by many virtuous people from numerous marketplaces for the purpose of buying and selling.

The world was adorned with vast clusters of dwellings where women skilled in subduing men resided; it was filled with water-birds, bees, and auspicious swans, as well as flocks of *kāraṇḍava* ducks and other aquatic birds, who took pleasure in tasting the honey dripping from the blossoming lotuses within many long, expansive ponds; it was frequented by domestic animals and others who were contented and accompanied by their beloved mates; and it was pervaded by celestial wish-fulfilling trees (*kalpavṛkṣa*) that were covered with swarms of bees clinging to masses of various fragrant flowers in full bloom, day after day.
In a brilliant jeweled pavilion surrounded by all kinds of fluttering banners, where cool and gentle breezes—respected by men who repeatedly offered what was desired—were blowing;
in its center illuminated by rows of jewel-lamps, adorned with canopies of various colors and hung with strings of pearls; its interior beautified by garlands of many-colored flowers;
its floor sprinkled with fragrant scented water; and filled with the sounds of thousands of auspicious women whose eyes were rolling with intoxication and passion.

For the attainment of one's desired goals, one should meditate upon the Beloved of Lakṣmī seated upon a lotus-throne at the foot of the Supreme Brahman—a throne as radiant as a thousand suns—amidst a ground of jewels where the pride of the rain-god Indra is cast down by the incessant showering of great gems. He is perpetually served on all sides by celestial maidens who move with swaying lotus-like hands holding beautiful chowries, whose broad and elevated breasts press against their slender waists, and whose sweet speech flows in a continuous stream. From his mouth, which exudes the nectar of supreme bliss, flows a splendor that is the cause of the universe, possessing the exquisite luster of a rising fresh blue lotus. One should thus contemplate Him for the fulfillment of one’s wishes.

The Lord, whose hair is thick and adorned with flowers, wears a crown of rubies; his forehead and nose are perfectly beautiful, and he is graced by playful, creeper-like eyebrows. His pair of large, tremulous eyes are deeply reddened, and he wears shimmering jeweled earrings. His glorious cheeks surpass the radiant redness of the bandhūka flower, and his lips are as crimson as that bloom. He brightens all directions with the splendor of his smile, and his charming face is slightly perspiring. His body is adorned with necklaces of pearls and other ornaments set with clusters of precious gems of flashing rays, and he is graced by the bristling of his body hairs.

His limbs were anointed with the liquid paste of camphor, agallochum, and saffron; he was naturally beautiful, endowed with ten arms that were rounded, thick, very long, and tender—arms whose number measured the very quarters of the sky. His pair of lotus-feet possessed the luster of red lotuses, and his heart was agitated by the pain of love. With his two lotus-hands placed upon his own lap, he was embracing his beloved Rukmiṇī, who sat there with her heavy, languid pair of thighs covering him. He, possessing the brilliance of pure gold, embraced his dear one, while she, with moist hips, firmly clung to the Lord with her two arms in a state of passionate attachment, her pair of lotus-hands resting upon his.

She was embraced by one who stood perfectly close to her, her body covered in horripilation as she shimmered with joy; her limbs were beautiful, adorned by drops of perspiration appearing like pearls shed under the guise of sweat;

the entire sequence of her sensory faculties was absorbed in him alone, and she was immersed in an ocean of bliss with limbs free from any agitation. She was also embraced by the dark-complexioned Jāmbavatī, who stood at his right side, clad in divine silken garments and unguents, adorned with every ornament, her body pierced by the arrows of Kāma, and her arms wrapped around him in red-hued affection.
He was embracing with his own arm her who stood close by him and possessed the aforementioned characteristics, while Kālindī embraced His back;

He, the All-pervading Lord, whose luster was like a dark blue cloud, held a lotus, a mace, a discus, and a conch in His four hands, while His lotus-face was pressed against the holes of the flute shining between two of His hands. He was surrounded on all four sides by gods, sages, and celestial beings, all filled with the weight of devotion and love.

Having meditated thus—[on Him] whose limbs are bent low by those praising with hymns, whose mind is fully intent on service, who eternally bestows the four aims of life, who is beyond the reach of mind and speech, who abides in His own splendor, and who is immersed in the ocean of the nectar of great bliss—one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity. At the conclusion of the recitation, having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other components, and having offered the recitation to the Lord, one should prostrate.
This is the mantra of Saṃmohana-Gopāla. Now, the mantra of Saṃtāna-Gopāla: "O son of Devakī, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O Lord of the Universe, grant [me]..."

"I have come for refuge to You, O Kṛṣṇa, the embodiment of this very method. Having performed three rounds of breath control (prāṇāyāma) with this mantra consisting of thirty-two syllables, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa): "Obeisance to Nārada, the Seer (ṛṣi)," on the head; "Obeisance to Anuṣṭubh, the Metre (chandas)," on the mouth; "Obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Deity (devatā)," on the heart. Having performed the pervasive placement (vyāpaka-nyāsa) on both hands with the root mantra, one should recite: "Obeisance to the Heart of Govinda, the Son of Devakī"; "Svāhā to the Head of Vāsudeva, the Lord of the World"; "Vaṣaṭ to the Tuft (śikhā) of Kṛṣṇa, who gives this very method"; "Tvā... [and so forth].

Having gone for refuge to Haṃsa, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the five-limbed mantras—*haṃ kavacāya huṃ* and *samastamantra astrāya phaṭ*—upon the fingers from the thumb to the little finger; then, without placing them on the heart and other limbs, one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: One should meditate upon the infallible Lord Viṣṇu, who holds a conch and a discus, is dark-complexioned, four-armed, resplendent with all ornaments, and clad in yellow garments. He is endowed with a peacock’s tail-feather, augmented by splendor, and bringing back the lost children to present them to the Brahmin, [anointed] with the nectar of compassion.

Having meditated thus: "The unborn one, the sole abode of perfect activity, four-armed"—by which [epithet] the mace and lotus are indicated; the visualization of the weapons is as follows: the first pair [of hands] are on the left and right upper [arms], and the other two pairs are on the first and second lower [arms].

But for women, [she should meditate on the Lord] seated facing her upon her own lap, on a pure red lotus, with dark hair, adorned with a multitude of blazing jewel-crests, possessing the luster of refined gold, and being embraced again and again with love out of the impulse of joy. A woman desiring a son should contemplate the enemy of Mura (Viṣṇu) as her own son. Having meditated in this way...

Having performed the recitation according to one's capacity and having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other factors at the conclusion of the recitation, one should offer the recitation. This is the mantra of Saṃtānagopāla. Now follows the Kṛṣṇa mantra known as Nigaḍachedana (The Breaker of Shackles):
"O Vasudeva, for the breaking of shackles, to Vāsudeva, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with this twenty-syllable mantra, one should assign:
"Salutation to the Ṛṣi Nārada on the head; salutation to the Gāyatrī metre in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the breaker of shackles, in the heart. Thus [it is said].

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with the previously mentioned ten-syllable Gopāla mantra beginning with *ā-cakra*, and having assigned the seers (*ṛṣi*) and other components, one should meditate as before on "the beautiful Vṛndāvana" and so forth. Having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to the rules, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should assign the seers and others again and offer the recitation. This is the Kṛṣṇa mantra known as "The Severing of the Shackles. Now follows the Kṛṣṇa mantra known as "The Enchantment of the World": having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the single-syllable mantra *klīṃ*, one should place [the seed syllables] on the head with "Salutation to the seer Nārada, the Enchanter," and on the mouth...

"Salutation to Gāyatrī Chandas at the heart; salutation to the deity Kṛṣṇa, the Enchanter, at the [heart]; salutation to the syllable *kaṃ*, the Seed, at the secret place; salutation to the Power (*śakti*) *iṃ* at the feet; salutation to the Pin (*kīlaka*) *laṃ* at the navel. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*), one should say, "The application is for the attainment of all my desired goals," and with palms joined in reverence, having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *klīṃ klīm* and so forth, one should meditate as follows: "At the root of the garden of ancient trees, shining with the Kalpa-trees..."

Seated upon the back of the great Garuḍa—who resembles the rising sun, who is the very form of the life-breath of the universe, and whose wings are spread wide—the Lord sits upon a magnificent jeweled lion-throne at Rāṣṭhalī. He has the luster of a Bandhūka flower, a complexion like that of the enemy of Tārṣava (Śiva), and holds in his eight lotus-like hands a discus, a conch, a goad, a vessel, a flower-arrow, a sugarcane bow, a lotus, and a mace. His two large, reddish, and glistening lotus-eyes are wide open and rolling; he is adorned with a crown of blossoming jewels and radiant gem-studded earrings.

Adorned with a lotus, resplendent with pearl necklaces, shining gems, bracelets, armlets, rings, tinkling bells, and anklets; decorated with red garlands and smeared with crimson unguent; radiant in garments of golden-hued silk; embracing his beloved Lakṣmī who rests upon the seat of his own left thigh; holding the seed-syllable (Vojā) in his left arm; her temple moist with intoxication; her limbs aglow and agitated by the intense passion of love; her body adorned with beautiful garlands and ointments, and graced with every ornament; [she whose] subtle... [is pure].

One should meditate upon the God who is the teacher of all worlds, the Truth and Bliss, who embraces with his left arm this Dawn (Taraṇī)—who is richly adorned with fine garments, whose beautiful lotus-face is graced by hovering bees that are her shimmering dark-blue eyes, and who holds a sugarcane bow; who is delighted by the supreme bliss of that union; who is surrounded by hosts of women from among the Suras, Asuras, lords of serpents, Siddhas, and Gandharvas, who are themselves afflicted by the arrows of Kāma and enriched by their excellent beauty; and who is seated upon the right and left thighs, beginning from the top and arranged in pairs in descending order.

One should meditate thus; having meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other components, offer the recitation to the Deity, and prostrate.

This is the mantra of Kṛṣṇa known as "World-Enchanting" (*jagatsaṃmohana*). Now, the Kāma-mantra: having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the single-syllable mantra *kliṃ*, one should perform the placement: "Salutation to the Seer Sammohana on the head; salutation to the Gāyatrī metre on the mouth; salutation to the Deity Śrīkāma on the heart; salutation to the Seed-syllable *kaṃ* on the private parts."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "OṂ *iṃ* Śakti, salutation to the feet; OṂ *laṃ* Kīlaka, salutation to the navel," and having performed the ritual placement of the hands and limbs (*kara-aṅga-nyāsa*) with *klāṃ klīṃ* and so forth, one should meditate as follows:

"I always contemplate the God who is the Mind-born (*Manasija*), whose abode is the red lotus, who is red with red eyes, exceedingly beautiful, wearing red garments, his body adorned with a multitude of ornaments such as a crown shining with jewels, holding in his hands the noose, the goad, the sugarcane bow, and flower-arrows—the all-pervading Lord. [The visualization continues] from the left upward... [and so on].

One should meditate on the weapons as follows: "The others [are held] in the two hands located below these [two]," and so forth. Having thus meditated, at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), one should perform the placement of the *ṛṣi* and other limbs, offer the recitation, and prostrate. This is the Kāma-mantra. Now, the Kṛṣṇa-mantra known as the Praṇava: having spent three watches of the night with the single-syllable mantra *Oṃ*, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; salutation to the Goddess Gāyatrī, the meter (*chandas*), in the mouth; salutation to Śrī Paramātman, the deity (*devatā*), in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *Aṃ*, in the secret place; salutation to the *Uṃ* [seed-syllable], in the feet."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Oṃ Ktaye Namaḥ" for the heart and "Oṃ Nābhomaṃkīlakāya Namaḥ" for the *kīlaka*, and having declared with palms joined, "This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the sake of my liberation," one should perform the six-limbed mantra (*ṣaḍaṅga-mantra*) as follows: "Aṃ Oṃ Āṃ Hṛdayāya Namaḥ" (to the heart); "Ī Oṃ Īṃ Śirase Svāhā" (to the head); "Uṃ Oṃ Ūṃ Śikhāyai Vaṣaṭ" (to the crest-lock); "Eṃ Oṃ Aiṃ Kavacāya Huṃ" (to the armor); "Oṃ Oṃ Auṃ Netrāya Vauṣaṭ" (to the eyes); "Aṃ Oṃ Aḥ Astrāya Phaṭ" (to the weapon). Having thus placed these mantras on the two hands from the thumbs to the palms, and having also placed them on the six limbs starting from the heart, one should meditate as follows:

I worship Viṣṇu, whose glorious body is stainless, who is clothed in yellow silk garments, who possesses the radiance of the sun due to his splendor rising in every direction, whose limbs are adorned with ornaments such as a crown, armlets, necklaces, girdles, anklets, neck-chains, and bracelets; who holds the discus, conch, lotus, and mace in his lotus-like hands; who is illuminated by the luster of the Kaustubha gem and adorned with jeweled earrings; and who is seated upon a full-blown lotus for the sake of attaining all prosperity—beginning from the lower left hand up to the lower right.

Having meditated on the visualization of the weapon extending to the hand, and having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other limbs, offer the oblation, and prostrate.

Thus ends the mantra of Kṛṣṇa known as the *Praṇava*. Now follows the mantra of Kārtavīryārjuna: *Phroṃ vrī klīṃ bhrūṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ śrīṃ huṃ phaṭ kārtavīryārjunāya namaḥ*. This nineteen-syllable mantra (which becomes twenty syllables when preceded by the *praṇava*, i.e., *oṃ*) is used for three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). Then, one should assign the limbs: *Oṃ datātreyarṣaye namaḥ* to the head; *Oṃ anu...* to the mouth.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Oṃ, salutation to the *ṣṭup* metre; Oṃ, salutation to the deity Śrī Kārtavīryārjuna at the heart," and having said with palms joined, "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of all my attainments," he should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) on both hands with the root mantra. Then, having placed the five-limbed mantras on the fingers from the thumb to the little finger: "Phroṃ vrīṃ, salutation to the heart; Klīṃ bhrūṃ, svāhā to the head; Āṃ hrīṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crown-lock; Kroṃ śrīṃ, huṃ phaṭ to the armor; Astra, phaṭ. [He then places them] on the eyes.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) upon the five limbs beginning with the heart of Vajra, and having made the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) on all limbs with the mantra "Oṃ, obeisance to Kārtavīryārjuna," one should perform meditation as follows: "May that Lord, the beloved of the earth, protect us incessantly— he whose body is revealed from all fear, who is illuminated by the light of the sun, whose neck is encircled by a golden garland, who wears red garments and a turban, who is adorned with various ornaments, who holds a bow and half a thousand arrows in his thousand hands, and who possesses half a thousand arms."

May that glorious Kārtavīrya protect you—he who is the sole lord of the island, whose splendor is equal to the sun, the end-maker of all the wicked, whose eyes are born from the lotus, whose abode is his excellent chariot, whose body is massive and most terrifying;
he who, wielding a bow in his hand, strikes terror into those who oppress the three worlds with its twang, and who swiftly acts to crush the lotus-feet of all rival kings.

Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's ability, and having assigned the *ṛṣi*, *chandas*, and *devatā* at the conclusion of the recitation, one should offer the merit of the recitation to the deity and prostrate. Thus ends [the section on] Kārtavīryārjuna.
Regarding this mantra, because its purpose is ritual action, there are many variations in the mantras and their meditations; however, these are not described here due to the bulk of the text.

[Thus ends the ninth chapter in the *Mantracandrikā* composed by Gosvāmin Janārdana, son of Gosvāmin Jagannivāsa. Thus concludes the Vaiṣṇava section. Now, the Saura mantras are stated. First, regarding the eight-syllabled Sūrya mantra: having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the mantra "Oṃ ghṛṇiḥ sūrya ādityaḥ," one should [place the hand] on the head.

Salutation to Devabhāga Ṛṣi; salutation to Gāyatrī Chandas at the mouth; salutation to Śrīsūrya Devatā at the heart. Thus for the daily [mantra]: *Satyatejojvālāmaṇi huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—salutation to the Heart. *Brahmatejojvālāmaṇi huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—salutation to the Head (*Svāhā*). *Viṣṇutejojvālāmaṇi huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—salutation to the Tuft (*Vaṣaṭ*). *Rudratejojvālāmaṇi huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—salutation to the Armor (*Huṃ*). *Agnitejojvālāmaṇi huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—to the Eyes.

Having performed the *ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* on the hands with the mantras: *yavauṣaṭ*, *sarvatejojvālāmahuṃphaṭsvāhā*, and *astrāyaphaṭ*, one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "I worship Him who has a body the color of the rising sun, adorned with armlets and earrings, seated upon a beautiful, red lotus, possessing two eyes, holding a pair of lotuses and granting fearlessness with His hands, and bestowing boons upon the Dānavas. This is the visualization of the weapons: in the two upper hands there are lotuses, and in the two lower hands, which are on the left side, are the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons. Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, [one should perform] the *ṛṣyādi* [nyāsa].

Having placed [the mantra] on the *kaṃ* (the head) and offered the recitation (*japa*) to the God, one should prostrate. Thus ends the eight-syllabled Sūrya-mantra. Now, the six-syllabled Sūrya-mantra:

having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the mantra "Khakholkāya svāhā," one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Obeisance to Brahmā, the Ṛṣi, on the head"; "Obeisance to Gāyatrī, the Chandas, on the mouth"; "Obeisance to Śrīsūrya, the Devatā, on the heart.

Then, the mantra "Sūkṣmarūpāya svāhā huṃ phaṭ" should be known to apply to the five limbs (from the heart onwards), ending with *svāhā*. [The sequence is: "To the subtle form, svāhā; *huṃ phaṭ* [on the heart]; *huṃ phaṭ svāhā* [on the head]; *sūkṣmatejase svāhā* [on the tuft]."

"Hāṃ śiraḥ sūkṣmakārāya svāhā! Śikhā sūkṣmavālāya svāhā! Kavacaṃ sūkṣmakāyāya svāhā! Huṃ phaṭ astrāya phaṭ! Having thus assigned these five limb-mantras (pañcāṅga-mantras) to the fingers starting from the thumb and ending with the little finger, and having likewise assigned them to the heart and other centers—excluding the eyes—one should perform the six-limb assignment (ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa) using the six syllables of the mantra and then meditate as follows: "One should meditate upon [the deity] who holds two red lotuses in his hands, displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, possessing the luster of a bandhūka flower, three-eyed, and beautifully adorned."

Having meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having performed the *nyāsa* of the Ṛṣi and other [limbs] at the end of the recitation, one should offer the recitation. This is the six-syllabled mantra of the Sun. Now, the seven-syllabled mantra of the Sun:

having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the mantra "Svaṃ Svasvoklāya Svāhā," one should perform the Ṛṣi, meditation, the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), and so forth, as in the previously mentioned eight-syllabled mantra of the Sun. This is the seven-syllabled mantra of the Sun. Now, the four-syllabled mantra: having performed three rounds of breath control with the mantra "Oṃ Hrīṃ Haṃsaḥ."

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to Brahmā, the seer, on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the metre, on the face; salutation to the deity Bhuvaneśvarī, who is the form of the glorious Sun, on the heart"; and having declared the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the hands with the mantras: *Oṃ* for the heart, *Hrīṃ* for the head, *Oṃ* for the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *Hrīṃ* for the armor (*kavaca*), *Oṃ* for the eyes, and *Hrīṃ* for the weapon (*astra*).

Then one should meditate as follows: "She whose crown shines with a thousand radiant jewels, illuminating the crescent moon; she who holds in her lotus-like hands the goad, the rosary, the boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness."

May she protect the universe—she whose breasts are very high, who possesses the luster of molten gold, and whose body, like a flash of lightning, illuminates the entire world from the hot season until the cold;

she who holds the discus and conch in her upper two hands, and other weapons in the first pair of lower hands. Thus is the visualization of the weapons. Having meditated thus, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity.

At the end of the recitation, having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other components, one should offer the recitation to the Goddess and prostrate. This is the four-syllable mantra. Now follows the three-syllable mantra: *hrīṃ hrīṃ saḥ*.

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas* with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Aja, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to Śrīsūrya, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart. Then, having uttered the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *hrāṃ hrīm*, and meditate thus: "I meditate upon the Lord of the Dawn, whose body is of a deep red hue, seated upon a crimson lotus, possessing three eyes and many ornaments, holding in his hands a pair of red lotuses, the wish-granting gesture (*abhīṣṭa*), and the gesture of protection (*abhaya*)."

Having meditated thus: "He who is to be served by the nakarasus, worshipped by all the gods," one should perform the recitation (japa) according to one's capacity. At the end of the recitation, having assigned the seer (ṛṣi) and other components, and having offered the recitation to the deity, one should prostrate. This is the three-syllabled mantra. Now follows the two-syllabled Sūrya mantra according to the Vijayā method: *Huṃ Aiṃ*. Having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma) with this mantra, one should assign [the parts] as follows:

"Salutation to Aja, the Seer, on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the metre, on the mouth; salutation to Śrī Bhānu, the deity, on the heart. Having thus assigned [the limbs], one should perform the application (viniyoga).

Having performed the *ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* on the hands with the mantras: "GAM" for the heart, "HSĀM" for the head, "HSĪM" for the crest, "HSŪM" for the armor, "HSAIM" for the face, "HSAUṂ" for the eyes, and "HSAḤ" for the weapon; one should meditate as follows:

"One should meditate upon the three-eyed, red Sun, seated upon a red lotus, holding a pair of lotuses, the gesture of granting boons (*vara*), and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhīti*) in his lotus-hands. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) of the *Śakti*, at the end of the recitation, having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other components, one should offer the recitation to the God. Thus ends the two-syllabled Sūrya-mantra named Vijayā.

Having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma) with the two-syllable mantra *haṃsaḥ*, and having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to the Goddess Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chandas*), in the mouth;

salutation to the Deity Śrī Paramātman in the heart," and having uttered the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *hsāṃ hsīm* and so forth, and then meditate as follows: "Gaurī, resembling a red lotus and gold, seated upon a lotus, holding in her hands a rosary, a chisel, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture of granting boons."

"Let us take refuge in that body which bears the crescent moon, whose form is both gentle and fiery, and which consists of half the portion of Girijā. Having meditated thus, having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other factors at the conclusion of the recitation, and having offered the recitation to the Deity, one should prostrate. This is another two-syllable mantra. Now follows the one-syllable Mārtaṇḍabhairava mantra: *hsauṃ*.

Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*): "Salutation to Brahmā, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; salutation to Nivṛt, the *chandas*, in the mouth; [salutation] to Śrī Mārtaṇḍabhairava in the heart."

Having uttered the application (*viniyoga*) as follows: "Obeisance to the Deity; obeisance to the *Haṃ* seed-syllable in the secret place; obeisance to the *Viṃ* power (*śakti*) in the feet; obeisance to the *Raṃ* pin (*kīlaka*) in the navel," one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the hands up to the little finger and upon the body from the heart up to the eyes with: *Hryāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *Hyīṃ śirase svāhā*, *Hyūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *Hyaiṃ kavacāya huṃ*, *Svaḥ astrāya phaṭ*, *Hryauṃ netrebhyo vauṣaṭ*. Then one should meditate as follows: [He who is] like gold, like a yellow *japā* flower, possessing three eyes...

One should meditate upon the four-faced [Lord], who holds in his lotus-like hands a rosary of pearls, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a trident, a string of beads, a lotus, a spear, and a goad, as well as a stainless skull-cup; who is embraced by his beloved; whose crown is beautiful with jewels like the sun; and who has eight arms and twelve eyes—as stated in the Nārāyaṇīya: "He has eight arms and twelve eyes. Regarding the objects held: the four beginning with the khaṭvāṅga are to be meditated upon starting from the upper right hand, and the four beginning with the lotus starting from the upper left hand. "Four-faced" means four mouths; "one-eyed per face" is the understood meaning, since it is said [in the same source]: "eight-armed and twelve-eyed."

Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other components and offer the recitation. This is the one-syllable mantra of Mārtaṇḍa-Bhairava. These are the mantras of the Sun. Now, the mantra of the Moon: *Soṃ somāya namaḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this six-syllable mantra, one should perform the assignment (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Bhṛgu, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; salutation to Paṅkti, the meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to Śrī-Candramas, the deity (*devatā*), on the heart; salutation to *soṃ*, the seed-syllable (*bīja*), on the private parts; salutation to *namaḥ*, the power (*śakti*), on the feet."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Maḥ" and having recited the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with "Sāṃ sīṃ," and then perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "May he who dwells upon a white lotus, possessing a splendor like crystal or silver, whose body is radiant with a long pearl necklace, who is beautiful with dark hair, and who holds a night-lotus and the boon-granting gesture in his two lotus-hands—may that moon, rising with its digits free from blemish, grant my desired prosperity. Having meditated thus on him holding the night-lotus and the boon-granting gesture in his left and right hands, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity.

At the conclusion of the recitation, having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the ṛṣis and other elements, one should offer the recitation. This is the mantra of the Moon. Now, the mantra of Mars: Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the eight-syllable mantra "Aṃ Aṅgārakāya Namaḥ," and having performed the placement as follows: "Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the ṛṣi, on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the meter, on the mouth; salutation to Śrī Bhauma, the deity, on the heart"; then, having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) using the seed-syllables ending in the six long vowels combined with "Namaḥ" and "Svāhā" and so forth, one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: [The meditation follows:]...

"I bow to Aṅgāraka, who is red, adorned with red garments and ornaments, whose left hand rests upon his knee and whose other hand on the shoulder is in the gesture of granting fearlessness. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other components, one should conclude. This is the mantra of Bhauma. Now, the mantra of Budha: "Vuṃ, obeisance to Budha"—having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with this six-syllable mantra, one should assign the components as follows: "Obeisance to Brahmā, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; obeisance to the *Paṅkti* meter on the face; obeisance to the deity Budha on the heart. Then [one should assign] "Bāṃ, Bīṃ... [and so forth].

Having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the syllable *Būm* and so forth, one should meditate as follows: "I always worship the wise Lord (Budha), who is well-adorned in yellow garments, whose left hand rests upon his knee, and whose other hand displays the gesture of fearlessness. Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having performed the placement of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other elements at the conclusion of the recitation, one should offer the recitation.

This is the mantra of Budha. Now, the mantra of Guru: *Vṛṃ Vṛhaspataye Namaḥ*. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with this eight-syllable mantra, [one should place] Brahmā as the seer on the head.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to *Namaḥ* in the mouth; salutation to the *Anuṣṭubh* metre in the heart; salutation to the deity, the venerable Guru," and having uttered the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *Vrāṃ*, *Vrīm*, and so forth, and meditate as follows: "The noble Guru, the god, should be meditated upon at night as scattering jewels, gold, garments, and other various objects from his right lotus-hand. Having meditated in this way and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should, at the conclusion of the recitation, perform the placement of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and the other components, and offer the recitation.

This is the mantra of the Guru. Now, the mantra of Śukra: "Śuṃ vastraṃ me dehi śukrāya namaḥ. Having performed *prāṇāyāma* with this eleven-syllable mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Ṛṣi, on the head; salutation to Virāṭ, the Chandas, in the mouth; salutation to Śukra, the Deity, in the heart. Then, having recited the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) on the hands and body with these mantras: "Śuṃ, salutation to the Heart; Vastraṃ, [salutation] to the Head; Me, [salutation] to the Crest (*śikhā*); Dehi, [salutation] to the Armor (*kavaca*); Śukrāya, [salutation] to the Eye; Namaḥ, [salutation] to the Weapon (*astra*)."

One should meditate thus: "I bow to Śukra, who is white-hued, adorned with an elephant's [white] ornament, wearing golden garments, possessing two hands that bestow streams of jewels, and whose form is pure consciousness.

Having meditated in this way and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other components at the conclusion of the recitation and offer the recitation to the deity. This is the mantra of Śukra. Now, the mantra of Śanaiścara:

Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the eight-syllable mantra, "Oṃ Śaṃ Śanaiścarāya Namaḥ," one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other components: "Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā, the ṛṣi, on the head; on the mouth... [and so forth].

*Oṃ, salutation to the Gāyatrī metre; salutation to the deity Śanaiścara in the heart.* Having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the mantra beginning "śāṃśī," one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*). As follows: "I salute Śanaiścara, who has curved fangs, is adorned with blue [garments], and whose left hand rests upon his left knee, while his other lotus-hand displays the gesture of fearlessness. Having meditated thus, having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having assigned the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other components, one should offer the recitation to the deity. This is the mantra of Śanaiścara. Now, the mantra of Rāhu: *Rāṃ, salutation to Rāhu*. This is the six-limbed [mantra].

Having performed three *prāṇāyāmas* with the *kṣara-mantra*, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to Rāhu, the Deity (*devatā*), on the heart. Having thus performed the placement and stated the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *rāṃ rīṃ rum*, and so forth, and then meditate. As it is said: "With palms joined in reverence, one should daily worship Rāhu, who is smoke-colored, serpent-bodied, deformed, with red eyes, and adorned with smoky ornaments. Having meditated thus, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity while maintaining that visualization.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the syllables *ṣya* and so forth, one should offer the recitation (*japa*) to the deity. This is the mantra of Rāhu. Now, the mantra of Ketu: Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the six-syllable mantra "Keṃ Ketave Namaḥ," one should perform the placement as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Paṅkti, the meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to Ketu, the deity (*devatā*), on the heart. Having thus performed the placement and uttered the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) with "Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ" and so forth, and then meditate as follows: "I revere Ketu, black in color, [black-faced...]"

Having meditated upon her as adorned with necklaces and other ornaments, with one hand placed upon her left thigh and the other lotus-hand in the *abhaya* (protection) gesture, and having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should at the conclusion of the recitation assign the *ṛṣi* and other limbs and offer the merit of the recitation. This is the *ketu-mantra*. Here, these planetary mantras are mentioned for the sake of convenience and not because they are included within the *pañcāyatana* (five-shrine) system.

Now, the fire mantras: having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the seven-syllable mantra "Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā," one should assign [the limbs]: "Salutation to Bhṛgu, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; to Gāyatrī, the meter, in the mouth..."

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Oṃ *chaṃdasena* namaḥ" at the heart; "Oṃ *agnaye devatāyai* namaḥ" at the secret place; "Oṃ *raṃ bījāya* namaḥ" at the feet; and "Oṃ *svāhā śaktaye* namaḥ," one should recite the application (*viniyoga*) and then the mantras for the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga-mantra*):
"Oṃ *sahasrārciṣe namaḥ* to the heart, *namaḥ*"; "Oṃ *svastipūrṇāya* to the head, *svāhā*"; "Oṃ *uttiṣṭhapuruṣāya* to the tuft (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*";
"Oṃ *dhūmavyāpine* to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*"; "Oṃ *saptajihvāya* to the eyes (*netra*), *vauṣaṭ*"; and "Oṃ *dhanurdharāya* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) on the two hands from the thumbs to the palms, one should also perform the placement on the six limbs beginning with the heart. Then, as for the meditation (*dhyāna*): "I praise the Lord who holds in his hands the *vara*, the *svastika*, and the *śakti*; who is seated upon a lotus, possesses three eyes, has the color of vermilion, is adorned with ornaments of refined gold, and whose matted hair is graced by fire. Having meditated thus and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having performed the placement of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other elements at the conclusion of the recitation, one should offer the recitation and prostrate. This is the seven-syllabled mantra of Fire (*Vahni*). Now, another mantra of Fire:

Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the twenty-five-syllable mantra: *oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ agne jātaveda iha āgaccha sarvakarmāṇi sādhaya svāhā*, and having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the heart and other limbs as before, one should perform the placement of the hands and the six limbs (*kara-ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsa*) with these mantras: *oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ hṛt agniḥ jātavedase ratā iha āvaha śikhā*, *sarvakarmāṇi kavacam sādhaya netram svāhā*, and *astram*. Then, having performed the meditation (*dhyāna*) as described in the previous mantra, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity.

At the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), having performed the placement of the *ṛṣi* and other limbs (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*), one should offer the recitation. This is the twenty-five-syllable mantra of Agni. Now, having performed the placement of the twenty-four [limbs] and so forth with the mantras:

"Arise, O Puruṣa! for the heart; "O Hari-pigala" for the head; "O red-eyed one" for the tuft (*śikhā*); "Grant me" for the armor (*kavaca*); "Bestow" for the eye; and "Svāhā" for the weapon (*astra*)—having thus performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), one should meditate as follows: [One should meditate on] the form of a horse emerging from the interior of the golden Aśvattha, the celestial tree, raining down heaps of wealth, grain, and jewels.

I bow to the Purifier (Agni), who possesses a divine form, whose pores are constantly filled with flames sprouting from his own body-hairs, who destroys the suffering of his devotees, and who bestows the fruits of Dharma, Artha, and Mokṣa.

Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having performed the assignment of the *ṛṣi* and other factors at the end of the recitation, one should offer the recitation and prostrate; such is the twenty-four-syllable mantra of Agni.
Thus ends the tenth chapter in the *Mantracandrikā* composed by Gosvāmin Janārdana Bhaṭṭa, son of Gosvāmin Jagannivāsa.

The *Kāśa* section (10), the chapter on the Sun, is completed. Now, the Śaiva mantras are being stated. First, the six-syllable mantra: *Oṃ namaḥ śivāya*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the sage Vāmadeva upon the head; salutation to the *Paṅkti* meter upon the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Sadāśiva upon the heart. Then, with palms joined in reverence, one says: "For the attainment of my fourfold human goals, this is the application (*viniyoga*). [Then the limbs: *Oṃ* to the heart, *na* to the head, *maḥ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*). *Śi*... [etc.]

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs on the hands using the six syllables—*namaḥ*, *svāhā*, and so forth—along with the mantras for the armor (*kavaca*), the two eyes (*netra*), and the weapon (*astra*), one should perform meditation as follows: One should meditate upon Śambhu, who is white like the foam of cow’s milk, possessing a luster equal to the silver mountain; adorned with a crown of matted hair shining with the beautiful crescent moon; bearing five faces, each with three eyes; clothed in a tiger skin and decorated with jewel ornaments; holding an axe and a boon-granting gesture (*vara-mudrā*) in his upper right hand, and holding a deer and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*) in his upper left hand.

Having meditated thus upon Śiva—the primordial of the universe, whose lotus-face is exceedingly serene, who is seated upon a lotus-throne, praised with devotion by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Indra, and other gods and asuras, the source of the world, possessing a universal form, the remover of worldly existence—one should perform the recitation (japa) according to the rules. At the conclusion of the recitation, having assigned the Ṛṣi and other limbs [of the mantra], one should offer salutation after completing the recitation. This is the six-syllabled mantra. Now, the five-syllabled mantra: Having performed three breath-control exercises (prāṇāyāma) with the mantra "namaḥ śivāya," one should assign: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Ṛṣi, on the head"; "To the Goddess Gāyatrī, the metre, in the mouth."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Obeisance to the Three-Vedic Metres" at the heart and "Obeisance to the Supreme Self, the Deity," and having declared "The application is for the sake of liberation" with palms joined in reverence, one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) using the five syllables and the entire mantra. Having meditated as previously described for the six-syllabled mantra, performed the recitation (*japa*), and at the conclusion of the recitation performed the placement of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other elements, one should offer the recitation and prostrate.

Thus ends the five-syllabled mantra. When joined with *māyā* (the syllable *hrīṃ*) at the beginning and end, the five-syllabled mantra becomes seven-syllabled; likewise, the six-syllabled [mantra] becomes eight-syllabled. In this way, there are two mantras.

Thus, *hrīṃ namaḥ śivāya hrīṃ* is this seven-syllabled mantra; *hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ śivāya hrīṃ* is the eight-syllabled mantra. Regarding these two mantras, the Lord of the Universe is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the meter (*chandas*) is said to be *Paṅkti*, and Umāpati is their deity. Having thus assigned the seer and so forth for these two mantras—the seven-syllabled and the eight-syllabled—and having stated "the application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of all desired goals" with palms joined, one should then recite: *oṃ hrāṃ oṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ naṃ śirase svāhā*.

Having performed the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the mantras: *oṃ hrūṃ maṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *oṃ hraiṃ śiṃ kavacāya huṃ*, *oṃ hrauṃ vāṃ netrāya vauṣaṭ*, and *oṃ hraḥ yaḥ astrāya phaṭ*, one should meditate as follows:

[He is] red like the *bandhūka* flower, adorned with a crescent moon as a crest; in his upper right hand he holds a trident, and below that, the gesture of granting boons (*varadamudrā*); [in his] left...

Meditating upon Him who holds a *ṛddhi* (prosperity) skull in His upper hand and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*) in His lower hand; who is embraced by the goddess whose hand holds a red lotus with Her left arm; whose body is radiant with all ornaments; who is filled with joy in the presence of the Goddess; who has a smiling face, three eyes, and is adorned with every ornament—having thus meditated, at the end of the recitation, [one should perform] the *ṛṣi-nyāsa*. (Note: The term *gaṇeśvara* refers to Nandin, as established in the *Liṅga Purāṇa* during the dialogue between Śiva and Nandin; for Nandin is the lord (*īśvara*) of the *gaṇa* named Pramatha belonging to Śiva.)

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the [syllables] beginning with *dikaṃ*, one should offer the recitation (*japa*). Thus end the seven-syllable and eight-syllable mantras. Now, regarding the mantra known as Prāsāda: having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the single-syllable mantra *Hauṃ*, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the sage Vāmadeva on the head; salutation to the Paṅkti meter in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Sadāśiva in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *Haṃ* in the secret place; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *Hauṃ* in the feet. Having thus performed the placement, one should say, "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of all desired goals," and with palms joined in reverence, [recite] *hrāṃ*.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) on the hands with the mantras: *Hṛt Hrīṃ*, *Śiraḥ Hūṃ*, *Śikhā Haiṃ*, *Kavacāya Haiṃ*, *Netraḥ*, and *Astraṃ Haḥ*, one should meditate as follows:

[One should meditate upon Him] adorned with five faces—pure white, lightning-like, dark blue, clear, and red—with three eyes in each face; decorated with a crown of matted hair (*jaṭāmukuṭa*) graced by the crescent moon as an ornament; resembling pure crystal; seated upon a lotus; possessing a serene lotus-face; and holding [attributes] with His lotus-hands, starting from the right...

One should meditate upon Lord Sadāśiva, blazing with various ornaments, holding in his left hands a crest-jewel (śikhaṇṭa), a banner (aṅka), a thunderbolt (vajra), a sword (khaḍga), a fire (tanayānala), a serpent (sarpa), a bell (ghaṇṭā), a lotus (mṛṇi), a noose (pāśa), and the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya).

Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (japa) according to one's capacity, one should assign the seer (ṛṣi) and other components and offer the recitation. This is the mantra known as Prāsāda.

Now follows another eight-syllable mantra: *Oṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ namaḥ śivāya*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (prāṇāyāma) with this mantra, one should place [the ṛṣi] on the head, saying: "Salutation to Vāmadeva, the Seer."

Having performed the placement [of mantras] with "Salutation to Paṅkti-chandas at the mouth" and "Salutation to the deity Sadāśiva at the heart," and having stated the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) starting with: *hrāṃ hrāṃ oṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *hrīṃ hrīṃ naṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *huṃ huṃ maṃ* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*, and so forth; then one should meditate as follows:

[One should meditate on him] whose body is red like a mass of sindūra, whose face is smiling, who has three eyes, whose head is adorned by the crescent moon shining upon his jeweled crown, and who holds an axe in his upper right hand.

Below that [hand], in his left upper hand, he holds a deer; below that hand, having respectfully placed the tips of her breasts—which are like dense clouds covered in yellow [garments]—upon his lap, she sits holding a red lotus in her right hand. He is seated upon a red lotus, resplendent with various ornaments, and fragrant with divine perfumes.

Having meditated thus, having performed the recitation (*japa*), and having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other [limbs], one should offer the recitation. This is another eight-syllable mantra. Now follows the thirty-six-syllable [mantra].

The mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti is: *Oṃ hrīṃ dakṣiṇāmūrtaye tubhyaṃ vadat-mūla-nivāsine dhyāna-eka-niratāṅgāya namo rudrāya śambhave hrīṃ oṃ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Śukra, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Anuṣṭubh, the Meter (*chaṃdas*), in the mouth; salutation to the Deity Śrī-Dakṣiṇāmūrti, in the heart; salutation to Oṃ, the Seed-syllable (*bīja*), in the private parts; salutation to Hrīṃ, the Power (*śakti*), in the feet. [Thus, for the sake of my fourfold human goals...]

Having performed the ritual application for the sake of accomplishment, with palms joined in reverence, one should recite: *Oṃ hrīṃ dakṣiṇāmūrtaye hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *Oṃ hrīṃ tubhyaṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā*; *Oṃ hrīṃ vaṭamūlanivāsine hrūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*; *Oṃ hrīṃ dhyānaikaniratāṅgāya hai kavacāya huṃ*; *Oṃ hrīṃ nābhorudrāya hrauṃ netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*; *Oṃ hrīṃ śambhave hraḥ astrāya phaṭ*. Having thus assigned these six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) to the two hands from the thumbs to the palms, one should likewise assign them to the six limbs starting from the heart.

Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa), one should meditate as follows: upon the delightful slopes of the Golden Mountain (Hemādri), frequented by Siddhas and Kinnaras; where the heat of the sun is warded off on all sides by the branches of various trees;
where flowering trees are embraced by networks of well-blossomed creepers; which is cooled by the breezes from waterfalls issuing from rock clefts;

where the quarters of the sky are made resonant by throngs of singing female bees, flocks of dancing peacocks, and swarms of warbling cuckoos; and which is inhabited by deer who have cast aside all mutual jealousy, along with the ancient parrots and other birds.

As he was meditating upon that wonderful, protective tree— ever-present for the three [worlds], served by the gods headed by Indra who had come for his service, towering in great height, radiant with fruits of ruby, adorned with dense leaves made of emerald,
decorated with hanging ornaments made of the nine gems, embellished with fragrant flowers born of water and land,
frequented by flocks of parrots chanting the Vedas and Shastras, and skilled at cutting away the torments of worldly existence— he reflected on it.

One should meditate upon the primordial Lord of the worlds, the imperishable Dakṣiṇāmūrti, seated upon the auspicious jewel-throne of Mūlasthāna; possessing immeasurable splendor, with a face like the autumn moon, being praised by hosts of sages desiring divine knowledge; resembling a mountain of silver, with a complexion as pure as the foam of milk, adorned with a beautiful crown of matted hair shining like a crescent moon;
seated in the Vīrāsana posture, intent on gazing at the tip of his nose, with a most serene lotus-face beautified by three eyes, and with his upper right arm...

Holding a book and the gesture of exposition (*vyākhyāmudrā*) in his lower left hand, and holding a deer in his upper left hand, which rests upon his left knee as he sits upon a white lotus; adorned with lordly serpents raised up by the special binding of his waist-cloth—having thus meditated upon Dakṣiṇāmūrti, who is surrounded by a multitude of sages, one should perform recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity. At the end of the recitation, having performed the placement of the *ṛṣi* and other factors, and having offered the recitation to the deity, one should prostrate. This is the mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti. Now, the twenty-two-syllable mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti: *oṃ namo bhagavate dakṣi...*

Having performed three breath-retentions (prāṇāyāma) with the mantra: "O Dakṣiṇāmūrti, grant me wisdom, svāhā," one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Seer (ṛṣi), on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the metre (chandas), on the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, on the heart; salutation to Oṃ, the seed-syllable (bīja), on the private parts; salutation to Svāhā, the power (śakti), on the feet; salutation to Medhā, the pin (kīlaka), on the navel. Having thus performed the placement and uttered the application (viniyoga): "Oṃ Āṃ Oṃ, salutation to the heart; Oṃ Hrīṃ Oṃ, svāhā to the head."

*Oṃ ūṃ oṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ; oṃ aiṃ oṃ kavacāya huṃ; oṃ auṃ oṃ netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ; oṃ aḥ oṃ astrāya phaṭ.* Having thus assigned the six limb-mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) from the thumbs to the palms of both hands, and having also assigned them to the six limbs starting with the heart, one should meditate as follows: [One should meditate on Him] seated in the center of a lotus, resembling the stainless autumn moon, bearing the Gaṅgā, His crest illuminated by the shimmering crescent moon, His lotus-face serene, possessing three eyes, a smiling countenance, wearing divine garments, and adorned with divine perfumes and garlands.

One should meditate upon [the Lord] adorned with various jewels, embellished by celestial garments and ornaments, holding a rosary of pearls in his upper right hand and the *jñānamudrā* in the lower right; and in his upper left hand a jar of nectar and a book in the lower left. One should contemplate him as being served by hosts of sages and munis, with his lotus feet shining upon the seat of the head of Apasmāra.

Having thus meditated, at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*), one should perform the placement of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other components, offer the recitation, and prostrate. This is the twenty-two-syllable mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti. Now, the nine...

The mantra of Kṣaroda Dakṣiṇāmūrti is: *Oṃ namāḥ śivāya oṃ*. Having performed three breath-control exercises (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Śukra, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to the Anuṣṭubh meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, on the heart. Having stated the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) on the hands and body: *Oṃ* for the heart, *A* for the head, *Namaḥ* for the tuft (*śikhā*) with *vaṣaṭ*, *Śivāya* for the armor (*kavaca*), [the syllable] *Na* for the eyes, and *Oṃ* for the weapon (*astra*). Then, [one recites]: "White as the foam of cow's milk," and so forth.

Having meditated as before, performed the recitation (*japa*), and assigned the *ṛṣi* and other components, one should offer the recitation and prostrate; such is the nine-syllable mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti. Now follows another nine-syllable mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti: "Oṃ aiṃ namaḥ klīṃ śivāya sauḥ. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other components as in the first nine-syllable mantra, and perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as follows: "Oṃ" for the heart, "aiṃ" for the head, "namaḥ" for the crest-lock (*śikhā*), "klīṃ" for the armor (*kavaca*), "śivāya" for the eyes, and "sauḥ" for the weapon (*astra*).

Whatever else one may do, one should first perform nine breath-retentions (*navākṣara*); this is the second *navākṣara*. Now, for the *Mṛtyuñjaya* mantra: having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the three-syllable mantra *Oṃ juṃ saḥ*, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the sage Kahola at the head; salutation to the goddess Gāyatrī meter in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *Oṃ* in the private parts; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *Saḥ* in the feet. Having thus performed the placement and stated the application (*viniyoga*), [one recites] *Sāṃ sīṃ*.

Having performed the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the syllables *sūṃ*, *se*, *sauḥ*, *saḥ*, *iti*, and *kara*, one should meditate as follows: One should contemplate Him who resembles pure crystal, seated upon a white lotus throne;

whose entire body is sprinkled with nectar falling from the crescent moon shining on the head of Kandarpa (Kāmadeva); whose left eye is half-closed; who holds the mudrā called Jñāna in His upper right hand and a rosary in His lower right hand;

and who holds a noose in His upper left hand and the Vedas in His lower left hand—one should thus meditate upon Him, the remover of the fear of death and disease. Having meditated in this way, according to one's capacity...

Having performed the recitation (*japa*) and assigned the *ṛṣi* and other components, one should offer the recitation. This is the *Mṛtyuñjaya* mantra. Now follows the *Aghorāstra* mantra: *hrīṃ sphura sphura prasphura prasphura ghora ghoratara tanurūpa caṭacaṭa pracaṭaka haha vama vama vaṃdha vaṃdha ghātaya ghātaya huṃ phaṭ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this fifteen-syllable mantra, one should assign: "Salutation to the sage Aghora on the head; salutation to the *ṛgvedic* meter (Gāyatrī) on the mouth; salutation to the goddess Aghorā on the heart."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Obeisance to Rudra, the deity; obeisance to the *huṃ* seed-syllable in the secret place; obeisance to the *hrīṃ* power in the feet," and having uttered the ritual application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) with the mantra: "Hrīṃ! Flash, flash! Heart! Quiver, quiver! Head! O you whose form is more terrible than the terrible! Topknot! Caṭa-caṭa, pracaṭa-pracaṭa! Armor! Ka-ha-ka-ha! Vama! Eye! Bind, bind! Strike, strike! Huṃ Phaṭ! Astra! Then one should meditate on the god who resembles a dark cloud, [fierce and] terrifying...

One should meditate [on the deity] who has a protruding tusk and three eyes, adorned with serpents, beautified by red garments and unguents, and holding in his right hands—in order from the top downward—a battle-axe, a sword, an arrow, and a trident; and in his other [left] hands, O Pārvatī, a *ḍamaru* drum, a shield, a bow, and a human skull. One should remember him as dark-complexioned for rites of desire (*kāmyakarma*), or red for subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), or white for the liberation from house-spirits and snakes, or resembling a pearl for rites of deliverance (*mukti*). Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should perform the ritual of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and so forth.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) and reciting [the mantra], one should proceed; this is the *Ghorāstra-mantra*. Now follows the mantra known as *Pāśupata*: *Oṃ śrīpaśu huṃ phaṭ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this six-syllable mantra, one should perform the placement (*vinyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the Seer Vāmadeva on the head; salutation to the Paṅkti meter in the mouth; salutation to the Deity Śrīpaśupati in the heart. Having stated the application (*viniyoga*), [one recites]: *Oṃ huṃ phaṭ*—salutation to the heart; *Śliṃ huṃ phaṭ*—*svāhā* to the head; *Yaṃ huṃ phaṭ*—*vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*); *Śuṃ huṃ phaṭ*... [to the armor].

Having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with: *kavacāya hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*, *netrāya vauṣaṭ phaṭ*, *huṃ phaṭ astrāya phaṭ*, one should meditate as follows: [One should meditate on] the Guru who has five faces and ten arms, with three eyes in each face; whose beard and hair resemble blazing fire; who possesses terrifying fangs; and who, with his right hands in the order starting from the top, holds a sword, arrows, a rosary, a spear, and an axe. With his left hands, he holds a shield, a bow, a water-pot (*kuṇḍikā*), a trident, and the staff of Brahmā (*brahmadaṇḍa*).

One should meditate upon the *Bhrāṇa* [mantra], which has a luster equal to the midday sun, blazing with various ornaments, adorned by the lords of serpents, resembling a mass of crystal, and bestowing all protection; having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other limbs at the conclusion of the recitation, offer the recitation, and prostrate. This is the mantra known as *Pāśupata*.

Now, the *Nīlakaṇṭha* mantra: *Proṃ Nīṃ Ṭhaḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this three-syllabled mantra, one should assign: "Salutation to the sage Aruṇa on the head" (*śiras*), and "to the *triṣṭubh* meter on the mouth" (*mukha*).

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Oṃ *chandase* namaḥ" at the heart for the deity Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha, and having uttered the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the placement of the five-limbed mantras (*pañcāṅga-mantra*) on the two hands from the thumb to the little finger, excluding the eyes, starting from the heart and so forth: "Hara-hara svāhā, *namaḥ* to the heart; Kapardine svāhā, *svāhā* to the head; Nīlakaṇṭhāya svāhā, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*); Kālakūṭa-viṣa-bhakṣaṇāya huṃ phaṭ, *huṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*); Nīlakaṇṭhine svāhā, *phaṭ* to the weapon (*astra*). [Thus, one should place these mantras on the five locations, beginning with the heart.]

Having also assigned [the mantras] to the limbs, one should meditate thus: one should meditate upon Nīlakaṇṭha, possessing the splendor of ten thousand rising suns; adorned with the crescent moon and the best of serpents in his massed matted locks; holding a garland of *jaya* flowers in his lotus-hands; bearing a trident in his upper right hand and a skull-cup (*kapāla*) in his upper left, while the *khaṭvāṅga* staff is in the hand below that;
resplendent with five faces, each face having three eyes; clothed in a tiger-skin garment; seated in the center of a lotus; and possessing an exceedingly beautiful form. Having meditated thus...

Having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other elements, offer the recitation, and prostrate. This is the *Nīlakaṇṭha* mantra. Now, for the *Mṛkṣāra* *Nīlakaṇṭha* mantra:

having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the mantra "Oṃ namo nīlakaṇṭhāya," one should assign the elements as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī, the meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to Nīlakaṇṭha, the deity, on the heart. Having thus assigned these, one should perform everything else as in the previously mentioned three-syllabled *Nīlakaṇṭha* mantra, and then conclude.

Now follows this eight-syllable mantra of Nīlakaṇṭha; then another eight-syllable mantra of Nīlakaṇṭha: *Oṃ nīlakaṇṭhāya svāhā*. Having performed the three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), reciting: "Salutation to the sage Aruṇa on the head; salutation to the Gāyatrī meter in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha in the heart. Then, having declared the application (*viniyoga*), one should recite: "Salutation to Nīlakaṇṭha, salutation to the heart, svāhā; salutation to the head, svāhā; *Oṃ* salutation to the tuft (*śikhā*), vaṣaṭ; *nī*..."

"Oṃ namaḥ śiraḥ (to the head), hūṃ namaḥ kavacāya huṃ svāhā (to the armor), namaḥ astrāya phaṭ (to the weapon). Having thus assigned these five-limbed mantras to the body from the thumb to the little finger, and having also assigned them to the heart and other parts excluding this [head], one should meditate as follows: "The God should be meditated upon as endowed with faces facing the east and other directions, which are white, yellow, red, and black respectively; holding in his arms the gestures of fearlessness (*abhaya*), an axe, a bow, and the *vāsuki* serpent. He is exceedingly beautiful, with Gaurī standing by his side. He performs, in sequence through his faces, the acts of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*), neutralizing poison (*nirviṣa*), paralyzing (*staṃbha*), and possessing (*āveśa*). [The mantra for the right face: "Dakṣi..."

Having meditated on the visualization of the weapons starting from the left lower hand up to the right lower hand, and having performed the *nyāsa* of the *ṛṣi* and other components at the end of the recitation (*japa*), one should offer the recitation and prostrate.

This is another eight-syllable mantra of Nīlakaṇṭha. Now, for the Cintāmaṇi mantra: having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the single-syllable mantra "Kṣmyai Ūṃ," one should perform the *nyāsa*: "Oṃ, salutation to Kaśyapa, the *ṛṣi*, on the head; salutation to Anuṣṭubh, the meter, on the mouth; salutation to Śrī-Ardhanārīśvara, the deity, on the heart; salutation to Kṣaṃ, the seed-syllable, on the private parts; [salutation to] the feet..."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Oṃ *ya-raṃ-śakti-ya*—salutation to the Name; *na-bha-u-maṃ-kīla-kā-ya*—salutation to the Nail," and having made the application with palms joined, saying, "This is for the attainment of all my desired goals" (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) on the hands as follows: *raṃ* for the heart, *kaṃ* for the head, *saṃ* for the tuft (*śikhā*), *maṃ* for the armor (*kavaca*), *raṃ* for the eyes, and *yaṃ* for the weapon (*astra*). Then one should meditate upon Maheśvara as follows: His left upper body is as red as coral, while his other (right) body is blue. His lofty crown shines with half of the moon and the Gaṅgā [coiled] like a serpent. He is Maheśvara in the form of Ardhanārī, manifesting the grace of amorous gestures and expressions. His other [half] is terrifying... (Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly.)
O Six-faced One, having meditated upon [the deity] holding a wondrous noose and a lotus in his upper left hand, and a trident and a human skull in his lower right hand;

adorned with divided garments, ornaments, garlands, and unguents—having thus meditated and performed the recitation (japa) according to one's capacity, one should perform the Nyāsa of the Ṛṣis and others at the conclusion of the recitation and offer the recitation. This is the Cintāmaṇi mantra. Now, for the Tuṃburudra mantra: having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma) with the single-syllable mantra *Kṣmyūṃ*, one should place [it] on the head.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to the Seer Hmaṇeṛṣi at the mouth; salutation to the Gāyatrī metre at the heart; salutation to the deity Śrī Tuṃburu-Rudra at the heart," and having declared the application (*viniyoga*) as "for the attainment of all my desired goals" with palms joined in reverence, one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) of the mantra upon the hands as follows: *Kṣmyāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *Kṣmyrīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *Kṣmyrūṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*; *Kṣmyraiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*; *Kṣmyrauṃ* to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *Kṣmyraḥ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. Then one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*) as follows: "The rising... [and so on].

O Śivā, one should meditate upon the god Śiva as follows: beautiful, four-faced, and three-eyed; bearing, in sequence with his four hands, a goad (*sṛṇi*) and a khaṭvāṅga staff in the upper right hand and a noose (*pāśa*) and a radiant skull-bowl (*kapāla*) in the lower right and left hands respectively; adorned with red unguents, ornaments, and garments; possessing a flattened nose; and enriched with priceless jewel-ornaments. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should assign the *ṛṣi* and other components and offer the recitation. This is the Tuṃburu [mantra].

Now the Kṣetrapāla mantra: *Oṃ kṣauṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ*. Having performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with this nine-syllable mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Namaḥ brahmaṇe ṛṣaye* on the head; *namaḥ gāyatrī chandase* on the mouth; *namaḥ śrīkṣetrapālāya devatāyai* on the heart; *namaḥ kṣa-bījāya* on the private parts; and *namaḥ śaktaye* on the feet. Having thus performed the placement and recited the application (*viniyoga*), one should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) beginning with *kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūm*, and then meditate as follows: [The meditation follows...]

O Goddess, one should meditate upon [the deity] who resembles a mountain of collyrium, who bears tawny matted locks on his head, who has three round and fierce eyes, who is adorned with terrifying serpents, whose face is formidable with protruding fangs, who possesses a fearsome form, who is naked, and who has two arms—holding a mace in his right hand and a skull-bowl in his left. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should, at the conclusion of the recitation, assign the *ṛṣi* and other limbs and offer the recitation. This concludes the mantra of Kṣetrapāla. Now follows the mantra of Vaṭuka Bhairava: *hrīṃ vaṭukāya*.

Having performed three rounds of *prāṇāyāma* with the twenty-one-syllable mantra: *dugdhāraṇāyakurukuruvaṭukāyahriṃ*, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to the Seer (Ṛṣi) Vṛhadāraṇyaka on the head; salutation to the Anuṣṭubh meter on the mouth; salutation to the Deity Śrī Vaṭukabhairava on the heart; salutation to the Seed-syllable (*bīja*) Hrīṃ on the private parts; salutation to the Power (*śakti*) Hrīṃ on the feet; salutation to the Pin (*kīlaka*) Āṃ on the navel. Then, with palms joined in reverence, state: "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of attaining the fourfold aims of human life (*caturvidhapuruṣārtha*)."

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of these mantras on the two hands, from the thumb to the palm—*ccārya (0) hrāṃ vāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *hrīṃ vīṃ śirase svāhā*, *hrūṃ vūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *hraiṃ vaiṃ kavacāya huṃ*, *hrauṃ vauṃ netrāya vauṣaṭ*, *hraḥ vaḥ astrāya phaṭ*—and having likewise performed the placement on the six limbs beginning with the heart, one should perform meditation as follows:

[He who is] resembling pure crystal, adorned with three eyes and blue lotuses, surrounded by curling locks of hair, his lotus-face beautifully smiling, [decked] with ornaments consisting of various jewels... what more?

The practitioner should meditate upon Śambhu in the guise of a young brahmin (baṭu), resplendent with anklets of tinkling bells, clothed in shining white garments, two-armed, holding a trident in his right hand and a wondrous staff in his left. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (japa) according to one's capacity, and having assigned the ṛṣis and other limbs at the conclusion of the recitation, one should offer the recitation and prostrate.

This is the mantra of Vaṭuka Bhairava. Now, the mantra of Tryambaka: "Tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam / urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt //" "We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity; may I be liberated from death, like a cucumber from its stalk, [but] not from immortality."

Having performed three rounds of *prāṇāyāma* with the thirty-two-syllable mantra beginning with "māmṛtāt," one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Oṃ, salutation to the sage Vasiṣṭha on the head; salutation to the *anuṣṭubh* meter in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya Rudra in the heart. Then, having recited the application (*viniyoga*), one should assign the limbs: "Oṃ, salutation to Agni, the heart; Oṃ, svāhā to Tryambaka, the head; Oṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three-eyed one, the tuft (*śikhā*); Oṃ, huṃ to Vasiṣṭha, the armor (*kavaca*); Oṃ, vauṣaṭ to the one whose virility is fire, the eyes; Oṃ, rudra..."

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs upon the hands with the mantras "daivatāya trāyaphaṭ," or alternatively, having performed the ritual placement of the six limbs upon the hands with the following mantras— "tryambakaṃ hṛt" for the heart, "yajāmahe śiraḥ" for the head, "sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanaṃ śikhā" for the crest-lock, "oṃ vārukaṃ iva bandhanāt kavacam" for the armor, "mṛtyor mukṣīya netram" for the eyes, and "māmṛtāt astram" for the weapon— one should meditate as follows: [upon the Supreme Being] who, with two hands, is bathing the head with the nectar-fluids from two jars, with two [other hands] is holding [them], and with two [others] is wearing a deer-skin and a rosary.

"I worship the three-eyed Lord Śiva, the beloved of Kailāśa, who holds two nectar-pots upon his hands placed on his limbs, who rests upon a pure lotus, and who wears a crown of the new moon"—having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, and having assigned the *ṛṣi* and other components at the end of the recitation, one should offer the recitation. This is the Tryambaka mantra. Now, the Gāyatrī:

preceded by the *praṇava*, there are the seven *vyāhṛtis*; beginning with the word *tat*, it consists of twenty-four syllables and is endowed with the head (*śiras*). With the head and the utterance of *svāhā*, it is upheld by all the Vedas.

This mantra with its essence has been proclaimed: *Oṃ bhūḥ, Oṃ bhuvaḥ, Oṃ svaḥ, Oṃ mahaḥ, Oṃ tapaḥ, Oṃ satyaṃ, Oṃ tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt svāhā*. Having performed three breath-restraints (*prāṇāyāma*) with this mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: "Salutation to Brahmā, the Ṛṣi, on the head; salutation to the Goddess Gāyatrī, the metre (*chandas*), on the face; salutation to the deity Śrī Paramātman, on the heart. Then, according to the method of the *praṇava* described in the section on Viṣṇu (page 62):

Having performed the *kara-ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsa* (the ritual placement of the hands and six limbs), and having meditated upon Viṣṇu as being of stainless splendor according to the prescribed method, one should then perform the following assignments: "Oṃ, salutation to the sages Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, Bhṛgu, Gautama, Kaśyapa, Viśvāmitra, and Vasiṣṭha" on the head; "Oṃ, salutation to the meters Gāyatrī, Uṣṇik, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī" on the mouth; "Oṃ, salutation to the deities Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, Guru, Varuṇa, Vṛṣa, and the Viśvedevas" on the heart. Having thus assigned them, [one recites]: "Oṃ bhūḥ to the heart; Oṃ bhuvaḥ to the head; Oṃ..."

Having performed the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the mantras: *Svaḥ* for the crest (*śikhā*), *Oṃ Mahah* for the armor (*kavaca*), *Oṃ Namaḥ* for the eyes (*netra*), and *Oṃ Tapah* for the weapon (*astra*), one should then perform the placement of the *vyāhṛtis*: *Oṃ Bhūḥ* Namaskāra at the heart; *Oṃ Bhuvaḥ* Namaskāra at the mouth; *Oṃ Svaḥ* Namaskāra at the right shoulder; *Oṃ Mahaḥ* Namaskāra at the left shoulder; *Oṃ Janaḥ* Namaskāra at the right thigh; *Oṃ Tapaḥ* Namaskāra at the left [thigh]; and *Oṃ Satyam* Namaskāra at the abdomen. Having thus placed them, one should meditate as follows: [The goddesses] are clothed in silken garments, adorned with all ornaments, their faces like blossoming lotuses, and radiant.

Adorned with *maṇḍalas*, their hearts purified by white sacred threads (*upavīta*), and possessing four hands made pure, with their lotus-hands displaying the gestures of fearlessness (*abhaya*), the rosary (*akṣamālā*), the water-pot (*abhaya*—variant reading: *varada*), and the boon (*vara*), one should meditate on them as thus described; then one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of Gāyatrī and the others. As follows: having performed the placement thus—"Salutation to Viśvāmitra, the Ṛṣi, at the head; salutation to the Goddess Gāyatrī, the Chandas, at the mouth; salutation to Śrī Savitṛ, the Devatā, at the heart"—one then [assigns]: *Oṃ* to Brahmā at the heart, *Oṃ* to Viṣṇu at the head, *Oṃ* to Rudra at the tuft (*śikhā*). *Oṃ*.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the mantras: "Oṃ to Īśvara" for the armor (*kavaca*), "Oṃ to Sadāśiva" for the eyes (*netra*), and "Oṃ to Sarvātman" for the weapon (*astra*), one should meditate as follows: "I worship Gāyatrī, who possesses three faces with the lusters of pearl, coral, gold, sapphire, and white; who is adorned with a jeweled crown bound by the moon; whose essence consists of the principles (*tattva*) and the letters (*varṇa*); and who carries in her hands, respectively, the gestures of granting boons (*varada*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*), a goad (*aṅkuśa*), a whip (*kaśā*), a radiant skull-bowl (*kapāla*), a triple-stranded cord (*guṇa*), a conch (*śaṅkha*), a discus (*cakra*), and a pair of lotuses (*aravindayugala*). [Note: *Kaśa* means a whip, and *guṇa* here refers to a trident (*triśūla*).]"

Beginning from the lower right hand and proceeding in order from right to left, one should meditate on the weapons in pairs, positioned one above the other. Having thus meditated and performed the recitation (*japa*) according to the prescribed method, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should complete the rite by assigning the *ṛṣi* and other factors of the *Gāyatrī*. This is the *Gāyatrī-mantra*. Any specific details regarding its ritual application (*nyāsa*) should be consulted in the *Śrīśivārcanacandrikā*.
Now follows the mantra known as Āgneya: *jātavedase sunavāma somamarātīyato nidahāti vedaḥ | sa naḥ parṣadati durgāṇi viśvā...* [nāvamiva svastaye]... [Note: The provided fragment ends mid-verse].
